automate.zh: 柜员机使银行的两个基本功能——

automatic.zh: 我的照相机是全自动的。

automatic.en: Littering results in an automatic fine.

automatically.en: Join now and you will automatically receive 50% off your first purchase.
automatically.zh: 现在加入，立即享受首次购物五折优惠。

automatically.en: Of course I automatically said yes.
automatically.zh: 当然，我脱口而出说是的。

autonomous.en: Galicia is an autonomous region of Spain.
autonomous.zh: 加利西亚是西班牙的一个自治区。

autonomy.en: Teachers are given considerable individual autonomy.
autonomy.zh: 教师被赋予相当大的个人自主权。

avail.en: We searched the whole area but all to no avail. Robbie had disappeared.
avail.zh: 我们找遍了整个地区但毫无结果，罗比失踪了。

avail.en: How many schools avail themselves of this opportunity each year?
avail.zh: 每年有多少学校利用这种机会？

available.en: Tickets are available from the box office.
Not enough data is available to scientists.
available.zh: 科学家没有足够的资料。

avalanche.en: Two skiers were killed in the avalanche.
avalanche.zh: 两名滑雪者在雪崩中丧生。

avalanche.en: The school received an avalanche of applications.
avalanche.zh: 学校收到雪片般寄来的申请。

avenge.en: He wanted to avenge his brother’s death.

avenue.en: The president wants to explore every avenue towards peace in the region.
avenue.zh: 总统想探索一切途径实现该地区的和平。

avenue.en: There are many avenues open to researchers.
avenue.zh: 研究人员有许多途径可供选择。

average.en: The age of the candidates ranged from 29 to 49 with an average age of 37.
The average cost of making a movie has risen by 15%.
average.zh: 制作一部影片的平均成本上升了15%

avert.en: The tragedy could have been averted if the crew had followed safety procedures.
avert.zh: 如果乘务人员按照安全规则操作，这场悲剧是可以避免的。

avert.en: Henry averted his eyes as she undressed.
avert.zh: 她脱衣服的时候，亨利把目光转向别处。

avoid.en: Road safety is taught to young children to avoid road accidents.
avoid.zh: 小孩子受到道路安全知识的教育，以避免交通事故。

avoid.en: It is important to take measures to avoid the risk of fire.
avoid.zh: 采取措施避免火灾风险很重要。

avoidable.en: Nearly 1,000 children die each year from accidents in the home which are avoidable.

await.en: Several men are awaiting trial for robbery.
await.zh: 几个人因抢劫正在候审。

await.en: A terrible surprise awaited them at Mr Tumnus’ house.
await.zh: 在图姆纳斯先生家，一件意想不到的可怕事情在等待着他们。

awake.en: She was still only half awake when I brought her a cup of coffee.
awake.zh: 我给她端去咖啡的时候，她还是半睡半醒的样子。

awaken.en: She was awakened by a noise at two in the morning.
awaken.zh: 凌晨两点，她被一个声音吵醒。

awaken.en: Bill slept a little until he was awakened to take his turn on guard.
awaken.zh: 比尔睡了一会儿，直到被叫醒去换岗。

award.en: The movie has won a number of awards.
Caprio won the award for best actor.
award.zh: 卡普里奥获最佳男演员奖。

aware.en: The children are aware of the danger of taking drugs.
aware.zh: 孩子们知道吸毒的危害。

aware.en: Mr Braley has been made aware of the need for absolute secrecy.
aware.zh: 布雷利先生被告知需要绝对保密。

awareness.en: Health officials have tried to raise awareness (=improve people’s knowledge) about AIDS.
awareness.zh: 卫生部官员努力提高人们对艾滋病的认识。

away.en: Dinah was crying as she drove slowly away.
away.zh: 黛娜一边哭一边慢慢地开车走了。

awe.en: He felt great awe for the landscape.
Kate gazed at the statue with awe.
awe.zh: 凯特满怀崇敬地凝视着塑像。

awesome.en: Their last concert was really awesome.
awesome.zh: 他们上一场音乐会真棒。

awful.en: He is a pretty awful driver.

awfully.en: It’s awfully cold in here. Is the heater on?
awfully.zh: 这儿非常冷，取暖器开了吗？

awkward.en: I hoped he would stop asking awkward questions.
awkward.zh: 我希望他不要再问令人难堪的问题。

awkward.en: There was an awkward moment when she didn’t know whether to shake his hand or kiss his cheek.
awkward.zh: 她不知道是该跟他握手还是亲他的脸颊，一时很尴尬。

axe.en: A hundred workers are facing the axe in a cost-cutting exercise.
MPs know there will be cuts in public spending but do not know on which department the axe will fall.
axe.zh: 议员们都知道要削减公共开支，但是不知道从哪个部门开刀。

axis.en: The Earth rotates on an axis between the north and south poles.
axis.zh: 地球绕着南北两极之间的地轴自转。

babble.en: I have no idea what he was babbling on about.
babble.zh: 我不知道他在唠叨些什么。

baby.en: She gave birth to a baby on Thursday.
baby.zh: 她于星期四产下一名婴儿。

bachelor.en: Gerald was 38, and a confirmed bachelor (=a man who has decided that he will never marry).
The Crown Prince was Japan’s most eligible bachelor (=a rich young man who has not yet married).
bachelor.zh: 皇太子是日本最理想的适婚男子。

back.en: I’ll be back in a minute.
Put that book back where you found it!

backbone.en: Farmers are the backbone of this community.
backbone.zh: 农场主是这个团体的中坚力量。

backbone.en: Stuart doesn’t have the backbone to be a good manager.
backbone.zh: 斯图尔特不具备一个优秀管理人员应有的毅力。

backdate.en: The pay increase will be backdated to January.

backdrop.en: The sea made a splendid backdrop to the garden.
backdrop.zh: 大海成了花园壮丽的背景。

background.en: Students with a background in chemistry will probably find the course easier.
background.zh: 学过化学的学生可能会觉得这门课程容易些。

background.en: It’s important to understand other people, people from different backgrounds.
background.zh: 要理解别人，理解那些来自不同背景的人，这是很重要的。

backing.en: She flew to New York to try to raise some financial backing for the project.
backing.zh: 她飞到纽约设法为这个计划募集一些资助。

backlog.en: It’s going to take us months to clear the backlog.
backlog.zh: 我们得花好几个月才能处理完积压未办的事情。

backup.zh: 什么时候都要有一个备用计划。

backup.en: Make a backup of any work you do on the computer.
backup.zh: 你在电脑上做的任何工作都要备份。

backward.en: She went without a backward glance.

backwards.en: She pushed me and I fell backwards into the chair.
backwards.zh: 她推了我一下，我便往后倒在椅子上。

backyard.en: The old man grew vegetables in his backyard.
backyard.zh: 老人在屋后院子里种了蔬菜。

backyard.en: Americans would probably react differently to the war if it was in their own back yard.
backyard.zh: 战争要是发生在自己的家门口，美国人可能就会有不一样的反应。

bad.en: I have some bad news for you.
I thought things couldn’t possibly get any worse.
bad.zh: 我想事情最坏也不过如此了。

badge.en: We were each handed a badge with our name on it.
badge.zh: 我们每个人都拿到一个徽章，上面有我们的名字。

badge.en: He now sees his wartime injuries as a badge of honor.
badge.zh: 现在，他把自己在战争中受的伤看成是一种光荣标记。

badly.en: The company has been very badly managed.
badly.zh: 这家公司的管理非常差。

badly.en: The novel was translated badly into English.
badly.zh: 这部小说被拙劣地翻成了英语。

baffle.zh: 这个问题把我彻底难倒了。
我们所有人都困惑至极。

bag.en: Don’t leave your bag in the car.
bag.zh: 不要把手提包留在汽车里。

bag.en: Just throw your bags in the back of the car.
bag.zh: 把你的行李放在车后部好了。

baggage.en: Check your baggage in at the desk.
What happens if my baggage is lost?
baggage.zh: 要是我的行李丢失了怎么办？

baggy.en: She was wearing jeans and a baggy T-shirt.
baggy.zh: 她穿着一条牛仔裤和一件宽松的T

bail.en: Carpenter is free on bail while he appeals his conviction.
bail.zh: 卡彭特取保获释，同时对判决提出上诉。

bail.en: She was murdered by a man who was out on bail for rape.
bail.zh: 她被一名犯强奸罪获保在外的男子杀害。

bait.en: The fish wouldn’t take the bait.

balance.en: I lost my balance and fell on my face.
balance.zh: 我失去平衡，脸着地摔倒了。

balance.en: Try to keep a balance between work and play.
balance.zh: 尽量保持工作和娱乐的平衡。

balcony.en: Has your flat got a balcony?

bald.en: Dad started going bald when he was in his thirties.
bald.zh: 爸爸在三十多岁的时候开始谢顶。

bald.en: He combed his hair and tried to hide his bald patch (=part of someone’s head where there is no hair).
bald.zh: 他梳了梳头，试图把头顶的秃块遮掩起来。

ball.en: Weiskopf hit the ball 330 yards and a cheer went up.

ballet.en: We’re going to the ballet tomorrow evening.
ballet.zh: 我们明天晚上要去看芭蕾舞演出。

balloon.en: Can you help me blow up these balloons?
balloon.zh: 你帮我把这些气球吹起来好吗？

balloon.en: He burst the balloon in my face.
balloon.zh: 他对着我的脸弄爆了气球。

ballot.en: The party leader is elected by secret ballot.
ballot.zh: 政党领袖是通过无记名投票选举产生的。

ballot.en: Workers at the plant held a ballot and rejected strike action.
ballot.zh: 工厂工人举行投票，否决了罢工行动。

ban.en: They are seeking a complete ban on nuclear testing.
ban.zh: 他们在寻求彻底禁止核试验。

ban.en: They imposed a blanket ban on beef products from Europe.
ban.zh: 他们全面禁止进口欧洲的牛肉制品。

band.en: The band was playing old Beatles songs.
band.zh: 乐队正在演奏披头士的老歌。

band.en: I grew up playing in rock bands.
band.zh: 我是在摇滚乐队里玩音乐长大的。

bandage.en: The nurse bandaged up his sprained ankle.
bandage.zh: 护士用绷带包扎他扭伤的脚踝。

bandit.en: They travelled 30 miles through bandit country.

bang.en: There was a loud bang outside the kitchen door.
bang.zh: 厨房门外传来砰的一声巨响。

bang.en: Stock markets started the year with a bang.

banish.en: I was banished to a distant corridor.
banish.zh: 我被赶到远处的一条走廊里。
成千上万的人被流放到西伯利亚。

bank.en: We have very little money in the bank.
bank.zh: 我们存在银行里的钱很少。

bank.en: I have to go to the bank at lunch time.

bankrupt.en: The firm went bankrupt before the building work was completed.
bankrupt.zh: 建筑工程尚未竣工，公司就破产了。

bankrupt.en: In 1977 he was declared bankrupt (=by a court).

bankruptcy.en: In 1999 it was revealed that he was close to bankruptcy.
When inflation rises, so do bankruptcies.
bankruptcy.zh: 通货膨胀加剧，破产个案也会增加。

banner.en: The onlookers were shouting, cheering, and waving banners.
banner.zh: 观众挥动着横幅，又是叫喊又是欢呼。

banner.en: She’d never felt the need to carry the banner of feminism.
banner.zh: 她从来都不觉得有必要打出女权主义的旗号。

bar.en: The hotel has a licensed bar.
bar.zh: 宾馆里有一家有售酒许可证的酒吧。

barbecue.en: We had a barbecue on the beach.

bare.en: She felt the warm sun on her bare arms.
bare.zh: 她感觉到阳光照在她裸露双臂上的暖意。

bare.en: The trees soon gave way to bare rock.
bare.zh: 不久，树也没有了，只剩下一片光秃秃的岩石。

barely.en: She was very old and barely able to walk.
barely.zh: 她年纪非常大，只能勉强走几步路。

barely.en: Mary had barely enough money to live on.
barely.zh: 玛丽的钱只够勉强度日。

bargain.en: There are no bargains in the clothes shops at the moment.
bargain.zh: 这阵子服装店里没有什么便宜货。

bargain.en: It’s an attractive little home, and I think it’s a bargain.
bargain.zh: 这是一个漂亮的小居所，我觉得是合算的。

barge.en: She ran outside, barging past bushes and shrubs.
barge.zh: 她跑了出去，磕磕绊绊经过一些灌木丛。

barge.en: She barged her way through the shopping crowds.
barge.zh: 她横冲直撞地挤过购物的人群。

bark.en: The dog always barks at strangers.
bark.zh: 这条狗总是对着陌生人叫。

bark.en: The police spent three months barking up the wrong tree on the murder investigation.
bark.zh: 警方调查这起凶杀案时方向不对头，枉费了三个月的精力。

barometer.en: The skin is an accurate barometer of emotional and physical health.
barometer.zh: 皮肤是反映一个人身心健康状况的准确指标。

barrel.en: The wine is aged in oak barrels.
barrel.zh: 这种葡萄酒是用橡木酒桶放陈的。

barrel.en: The manager has us over a barrel – either we work on a Saturday or we lose our jobs.
barrel.zh: 经理迫使我们就范，要么星期六上班，要么丢掉工作。

barren.en: Thousands of years ago the surface was barren desert.
barren.zh: 很久很久以前，地面还是一片荒漠。

barren.en: The sports hall was a rather barren concrete building.
barren.zh: 体育馆是一幢了无生气的混凝土建筑。

barricade.en: The fans were kept back behind barricades.
barricade.zh: 歌迷们被拦在路障后面。

barricade.en: During the riots, some of the prisoners barricaded their cells.
barricade.zh: 暴动期间，有些囚犯把牢房堵了起来。

barrier.en: He advocated the removal of trade barriers.
Problems with childcare remain the biggest barrier to women succeeding at work.
barrier.zh: 照顾子女问题依然是女性争取事业成功的最大障碍。

barter.en: I had to barter with the locals for food.
barter.zh: 我只得和当地人换点食物。

barter.en: They bartered their grain for salt.

base.en: The paper had intended to base itself in London.
base.zh: 这家报社原来打算把总部设在伦敦。

base.en: The new organization will be based in Dallas.
base.zh: 这个新的机构总部将设在达拉斯。

basic.zh: 他们所掌握的知识是相当初级的。

basically.en: Well, basically, it’s a matter of filling in a few forms.
basically.zh: 嗯，其实也就是填几张表的事。

basin.en: Fill the basin with the cake mixture.

basis.en: Their claim had no basis in fact (=it was not true).
basis.zh: 他们的说法没有事实根据。

basis.en: Bread forms the basis of their daily diet.
basis.zh: 面包是他们日常饮食中的主食。

bask.en: Lizards were basking in the morning sun.
bask.zh: 蜥蜴正在享受早晨的阳光。

bask.en: Tenerife was basking in afternoon sunshine as they arrived.
bask.zh: 他们到达的时候，特内里费正沐浴在午后的阳光中。

bat.en: She went to see a solicitor off her own bat.
He said yes right off the bat.

batch.en: Every day another batch of papers reaches the manager, demanding his attention.
batch.zh: 每天都有一批新的文件交到经理手里，要他处理。

batch.en: She was in the kitchen taking a batch of bread out of the oven.
batch.zh: 她在厨房里把一批面包从烤箱里取出来。

bath.en: After a week of camping, I really needed a bath.
bath.zh: 我露营了一个星期，实在得洗个澡了。

bath.en: I’ll have a bath and go to bed.

bathe.en: I bathed, washed my hair, and got dressed.
bathe.zh: 我洗了澡，洗了头，然后穿上衣服。

bathe.en: He bathed the children and put them to bed.
bathe.zh: 他给孩子们洗了澡，然后把他们弄上床。

bathroom.en: I really need to go to the bathroom (=use a toilet).

batter.en: As a child, she was battered by her father.
batter.zh: 她小时候遭受过父亲的殴打。

battery.en: You have to take the top off to change the batteries.
battery.zh: 你得把顶盖拿掉才能更换电池。

battery.en: When the red light comes on, you should recharge the battery.
battery.zh: 红灯亮起的时候你就应该给电池充电了。

battle.en: Her son was killed in battle.
Scientology has fought long battles for acceptance as a religion.
battle.zh: 科学论派为使人们承认它是一种宗教而进行了长期的斗争。

battlefield.en: Education has become a political battleground.
battlefield.zh: 教育问题已经变成了人们热烈争论的政治话题。

bay.en: A thick wall keeps the noise at bay.
bay.zh: 一道厚实的墙挡住了声音。

bay.en: Reporters began baying for the president’s blood (=demanding that he be punished).
bay.zh: 记者开始大声疾呼，要求给予总统惩罚。

be.en: Don’t disturb me while I’m working.
be.zh: 我工作的时候不要打扰我。

be.en: They’ve been asking a lot of questions.
be.zh: 他们已经问了许多问题。

beacon.en: The education program offers a beacon of hope to these children.
beacon.zh: 这项教育计划为这些儿童燃起了希望之光。

bead.en: She wore a string of green glass beads around her neck.
bead.zh: 她脖子上戴着一串绿色的玻璃珠子。

bead.en: Beads of sweat trickled down his face.

beam.en: Our guesses were way off beam.
Sherman looked at his sons and beamed proudly.
beam.zh: 谢尔曼看着儿子们，自豪地笑着。

bean.en: She’s full of beans this morning.

bear.en: She was afraid she wouldn’t be able to bear the pain.
bear.zh: 她恐怕自己忍受不了这种痛苦。

bear.en: Overcrowding makes prison life even harder to bear.
bear.zh: 过度拥挤使监狱生活更加难以忍受。

bearing.en: Exercise has a direct bearing on how healthy you are.
bearing.zh: 锻炼直接影响你的身体状况。

bearing.en: I completely lost my bearings in the dark.
bearing.zh: 我在黑暗中完全迷失了方向。

beast.en: A city at night is a very different beast.
beast.zh: 夜晚的城市又别有一番景象。

beat.en: Labour easily beat the Conservatives in the last election.
beat.zh: 工党在上一届选举中轻松击败保守党。

beautiful.en: She was even more beautiful than I had remembered.

beauty.en: Millions of dollars are spent each year on beauty products.
beauty.zh: 每年都有上千万的钱花在美容产品上。

beauty.en: She was considered a great beauty in her youth.
beauty.zh: 她年轻时被视为大美人。

beaver.en: He’s been beavering away at his homework for hours.
beaver.zh: 他埋头做作业已经有几个小时了。

because.en: We didn’t enjoy the day because the weather was so awful.
because.zh: 那天我们很不尽兴，因为天气实在太糟。

because.en: Hubert never experienced any fear, and this was partly because he was not particularly intelligent.
because.zh: 休伯特从来都没有害怕的感觉，部分原因是他这人不大聪明。

become.en: Slowly my eyes became accustomed to the darkness.
become.zh: 我的眼睛渐渐适应了黑暗。

bed.en: You should go to bed early.

bedroom.en: They’ve just bought a new four-bedroomed house in Edinburgh.
bedroom.zh: 他们刚在爱丁堡买了一幢有四间卧室的新房子。

bee.en: Dad’s got a bee in his bonnet about saving electricity.
She thought the party was just the bee’s knees.
bee.zh: 她觉得这次聚会棒极了。

beef.en: We have both dairy and beef cattle on the farm.
beef.zh: 我们农场里奶牛和菜牛都有。

beef.en: OK, so what’s the beef this time?
beef.zh: 好了，这一次又有什么苦要诉？

beer.en: We sell draught beer (=beer served from a large container, not a bottle).

beetle.en: He went beetling off down the corridor.
beetle.zh: 他从走廊急匆匆地走掉了。

befit.en: As befits a castle of such national importance, there are many stories connected with its history.
befit.zh: 这是一个对国家而言如此重要的古堡，理所当然流传着许许多多和它有关的历史故事。

before.en: I saw her a few days before she died.
before.zh: 她去世的前几天我见过她。

beforehand.en: The police need to be briefed beforehand on how to deal with this sort of situation.
beforehand.zh: 需要事先告诉警察这种情况怎样处理。

beforehand.en: When you give a speech, it’s natural to feel nervous beforehand.
beforehand.zh: 你在演讲之前感到紧张是很自然的。

befriend.en: They befriended me when I first arrived in London as a student.
befriend.zh: 我初到伦敦求学时，他们待我如同朋友。

beg.en: She begged and pleaded with them until they finally agreed.
beg.zh: 她一再恳求，后来他们终于同意了。

beg.en: She fought back the sudden urge to run to him and beg his forgiveness.
beg.zh: 她突然很想冲上去请求他原谅，但是她忍住了。

beggar.en: They showed a lack of common sense that beggars belief.
beggar.zh: 他们连常识都不懂，让人没法相信。

beggar.en: Why should he beggar himself for you?
beggar.zh: 他为什么要为你受穷呢？

begin.zh: 大家都到齐了，我们就开始吧。

begin.en: In the third year, students begin the study of classical Chinese.
begin.zh: 学生在三年级开始学古代汉语。

beginning.en: She’s been here since the beginning of the year.
There’s a short poem at the beginning of every chapter.
beginning.zh: 每一章的开头都有一首短诗。

behalf.en: She asked the doctor to speak to her parents on her behalf.
behalf.zh: 她请医生代她同她父母谈谈。

behalf.en: On behalf of everyone here, may I wish you a very happy retirement.
behalf.zh: 请允许我代表在座的各位祝你退休后生活愉快。

behave.en: She behaved in a very responsible way.
I think he behaved disgracefully towards you.
behave.zh: 我觉得他对你太不像话了。

behaviour.en: It is important to reward good behaviour.
behaviour.zh: 表现好要给予奖励，这是很重要的。

behaviour.en: She complained of her boss’s inappropriate behavior towards her.
behaviour.zh: 她抱怨说老板对她有不规矩行为。

behind.en: I turned to speak to the person standing behind me.
behind.zh: 我转身和站在我后面的那人说话。

behind.en: Someone could easily creep up behind us.
behind.zh: 很可能有人跟在我们后面。

being.en: The whole of her being had been taken over by a desire to return to her homeland.
being.zh: 她的整个身心都被回乡的念头占据了。

being.en: Being a quiet sort of person, I didn’t want to get involved.
being.zh: 我是个喜欢清静的人，所以不想介入。

belie.en: Her pleasant manner belied her true character.
belie.zh: 她讨人喜欢的举止掩饰了她真实的个性。

belie.en: His cheerful smile belied his words.
belie.zh: 他那开心的笑容证明他的话是假的。

belief.en: Thieves broke into the building in the mistaken belief that there was expensive computer equipment inside.
belief.zh: 窃贼们闯入大楼，误以为里面有昂贵的电脑设备。

belief.en: If you’re selling, you have to have genuine belief in the product.
belief.zh: 如果你在销售某个产品，就必须对所售产品真正有信心。

believable.zh: 那样的设想完全是可信的。

believe.en: You shouldn’t believe everything you read.
believe.zh: 你不应尽信书上看来的东西。

believe.en: I believed him, even though his story sounded unlikely.
believe.zh: 我相信了他，尽管他的话听上去难以置信。

bell.en: He rang the bell and waited for someone to answer the door.
bell.zh: 他按了门铃，等着有人来开门。

bell.en: The bell went and everyone rushed out of the classroom.
bell.zh: 铃声一响，大家都冲出了教室。

bellow.zh: 托尼正在吆喝着发号施令。

bellow.en: His voice rose to a bellow.
bellow.zh: 他提高声音，咆哮了起来。

belly.en: She was lying on her belly.

belong.en: Put the chair back where it belongs.
I worked there for five years but never really felt I belonged.
belong.zh: 我在那里工作了五年，但是从来没有真正觉得自己属于那里。

beloved.en: He never recovered from the death of his beloved daughter.
beloved.zh: 他一直没有走出失去爱女的阴影。

beloved.en: He’s always talking about his beloved computer!
beloved.zh: 他老是在谈论他的宝贝电脑！

below.en: Water was dripping onto the floor below.
I could hear voices in the courtyard below my window.
below.zh: 我能听到院子里有人在我的窗下说话。

belt.en: That was a bit below the belt, Paul.
belt.zh: 保罗，那样做有点不公平。

bemoan.en: He was bemoaning the fact that lawyers charge so much.

bench.en: We sat on a park bench.
bench.zh: 我们坐在公园的长椅上。

bench.en: Would the prisoner please approach the bench?
bench.zh: 请犯人走近法官席好吗？

beneath.en: The dolphins disappeared beneath the waves.
Jo enjoyed feeling the warm sand beneath her feet.
beneath.zh: 乔很喜欢脚下踩着温暖沙子的感觉。

beneficial.en: Cycling is highly beneficial to health and the environment.
beneficial.zh: 骑自行车对于身体和环境都大有裨益。

beneficiary.en: The rich were the main beneficiaries of the tax cuts.
beneficiary.zh: 富人是这次减税的主要受益者。

beneficiary.en: He was the chief beneficiary of his father’s will.
beneficiary.zh: 他是他父亲遗嘱的主要受益人。

benefit.en: I never had the benefit of a university education.
The new credit cards will be of great benefit to our customers.
benefit.zh: 新信用卡将大大方便我们的客户。

benevolent.en: A benevolent uncle paid for her to have music lessons.
benevolent.zh: 一位叔叔慷慨解囊，出钱供她上音乐课。

benign.en: He shook his head in benign amusement.
benign.zh: 他被逗乐了，和蔼地摇了摇头。

bent.en: Stand with your knees slightly bent.
He breathed in deeply, bent double in pain (=with the top part of your body leaning forward towards your legs).
bent.zh: 他深深地吸着气，痛得直不起腰来。

beset.en: The business has been beset with financial problems.
beset.zh: 该企业为财务问题所困扰。

beside.en: Wendy came up and sat beside me.
beside.zh: 温迪走过来，坐在我身边。

beside.en: I was standing right beside her at the time.
beside.zh: 当时我就站在她的旁边。

besides.en: I need the money. And besides, when I agree to do something, I do it.
besides.zh: 我需要这笔钱，而且，我一旦答应做什么事情就会做到。

besides.en: Moreover, smoking is linked with heart disease and strokes.
besides.zh: 此外，吸烟还与心脏病和中风有关联。

besiege.en: In April 655, Osman’s palace was besieged by rebels.
Miller was besieged by press photographers.
besiege.zh: 米勒被摄影记者团团围住。

best.en: He won the best actor award.
What’s the best way to cook this fish?

best-seller.en: His new book went straight to number one on the best-seller list.
best-seller.zh: 他的新书跃居畅销书榜首。

best-seller.en: The game is already a bestseller in Japan.
best-seller.zh: 这个游戏在日本已经很畅销。

bet.en: How much do you want to bet?
He bet me £10 that I wouldn’t do it.

betray.en: He felt that she had betrayed him.
What kind of man would betray his own sister to the police?
betray.zh: 向警方出卖自己的妹妹，那是什么样的人啊？

betrayal.en: She felt a great sense of betrayal.
betrayal.zh: 她有一种强烈的被出卖的感觉。

better.en: Your stereo is better than mine.
There must be a better way to do this.
better.zh: 一定还有更好的办法来做这件事。

between.en: I sat down between Sue and Jane.
between.zh: 我在苏和简中间坐了下来。

between.en: The ball rolled between his feet.
between.zh: 球在他两脚之间滚来滚去。

beware.en: They should beware of making hasty decisions.
beware.zh: 他们应该当心不要作出仓促的决定。

bewilder.en: He was bewildered by his daughter’s reaction.
bewilder.zh: 他被女儿的反应弄糊涂了。

beyond.en: They crossed the mountains and headed for the valleys beyond.
beyond.zh: 他们翻过山，向更远处的山谷进发。

beyond.en: Beyond the river, cattle were grazing.

bias.zh: 对学生的评估都是公正的。

bias.en: It’s clear that the company has a bias against women and minorities.
bias.zh: 这家公司很明显对女性和少数族裔抱有偏见。

biblical.en: The disease dates back to biblical times.
biblical.zh: 这种疾病在《圣经》时代就已存在。

biblical.en: This could result in an environmental disaster of biblical proportions.
biblical.zh: 这可能会导致极其严重的环境灾难。

bicycle.en: Can James ride a bicycle yet?
bicycle.zh: 詹姆斯会骑自行车了吗？
他们去哪里都骑自行车。

bid.en: They put in a bid for the house.
bid.zh: 他们出了一个价钱买这幢房子。

bid.en: We’ve made a bid of nearly £400 million for the company.
bid.zh: 我们出价近四亿英镑收购那家公司。

bidding.en: The bidding was brisk and sales went well.
bidding.zh: 买家踊跃出价，拍卖会进行顺利。

big.zh: 我需要一张大一点的桌子。

big.en: She had a big grin on her face.
big.zh: 她脸上挂着大大的笑容。

bike.en: Let’s go for a bike ride.
bike.zh: 我们去骑会儿自行车吧。

bilingual.en: The report proposed bilingual education in schools.
bilingual.zh: 报告建议在学校中实行双语教学。
他们的孩子会说两种语言。

bill.en: The bill for the repairs came to $650.
Have you paid the phone bill?

billion.en: The final cost could be as much as one billion dollars.
billion.zh: 最后的费用可能高达十亿美元。

billion.en: Overseas debt is a staggering £16 billion.

bind.en: They bound my arms and legs with rope.
bind.zh: 他们用绳子绑住我的手臂和腿。

bind.en: The pile of newspapers was bound with string.

binge.en: Ken’s gone on a binge with his mates.
binge.zh: 肯和他的伙伴们一起饮酒作乐去了。

binge.en: Whenever she’s depressed, she binges on chocolates.
binge.zh: 每当情绪低落时她就狂吃巧克力。

biodegradable.en: This carton is made of biodegradable plastic.
biodegradable.zh: 这盒子是用生物降解塑料做的。

biography.zh: 鲍斯韦尔为约翰逊博士写的传记

biological.en: Depression is both biological and psychological.
biological.zh: 抑郁症与生理和心理都有关系。

bird.en: The dawn was filled with the sound of birds.
bird.zh: 黎明时分，鸟鸣声不绝于耳。

bird.en: A little bird told me that you’ve got engaged.
bird.zh: 有人告诉我说你订婚了。

birth.en: Patsy was celebrating last night after giving birth to twins.
birth.zh: 帕齐生下一对双胞胎，昨天晚上在庆祝。

birth.en: Congratulations on the birth of your daughter!

birthday.en: My aunt called to wish me a happy birthday.
birthday.zh: 我姑妈打电话来祝我生日快乐。

birthplace.zh: 埃文河畔的斯特拉特福是莎士比亚的出生地。

birthplace.en: New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz.
birthplace.zh: 新奥尔良是爵士乐的发源地。

birthright.en: Freedom of speech is every American’s birthright.
birthright.zh: 言论自由是每一个美国人与生俱来的权利。

biscuit.en: I’ve heard some excuses, but this really takes the biscuit!
biscuit.zh: 我也听过一些借口，可这个借口也太离谱了！

bit.en: Could you turn the TV up a bit?
bit.zh: 你把电视机稍微开响点儿好吗？

bitch.en: The silly bitch went and told the police.
bitch.zh: 那个蠢婆娘去报告了警察。

bite.en: The dog bit him and made his hand bleed.
bite.zh: 那只狗把他的手咬出血了。

bite.en: She bit into a croissant and took a sip of coffee.
bite.zh: 她咬了一口牛角面包，啜了一口咖啡。

bitter.en: I feel very bitter about it.
If he failed, it would be a bitter disappointment to his parents.
bitter.zh: 如果他不成功，他父母会伤心失望。

bitterly.en: He complained bitterly about his exam grades.
bitterly.zh: 他悲叹自己的考试成绩不好。

black.en: It was still pitch black (=very dark) out.
Over half the students are black.
black.zh: 有超过一半的学生是黑人。

blacken.en: The thunder became louder and the sky blackened.
blacken.zh: 雷声更响，天色也黑了下来。

blackmail.en: She had already tried emotional blackmail (=tried to make him feel guilty) to stop him leaving.
blackmail.zh: 她试过以情相迫，不让他离开。

blackmail.en: He was jailed for four years for blackmailing gay businessmen.
blackmail.zh: 他因敲诈同性恋商人而入狱四年。

blackout.en: As the crisis worsened, the authorities imposed a news blackout.
blackout.zh: 危机逐渐加深，当局实行了新闻封锁。

blade.en: The blade of the knife flashed in the moonlight.

blame.en: Don’t blame me – it’s not my fault.
I blame his mother. She does everything for him.
blame.zh: 怪他母亲不好，她什么事都要为他做。

blank.en: Zoe looked at me with a blank expression.

blanket.en: The hills were covered with a blanket of snow.
blanket.zh: 群山覆盖着厚厚的白雪。

blanket.en: The trial was held under a blanket of secrecy.

blast.en: A blast of cold air swept through the hut.
Thirty-six people died in the blast.

blaze.en: It took almost 100 firemen to bring the blaze under control.
Helicopters were used to help fight the blaze.
blaze.zh: 出动了直升机来协助灭火。

bleach.zh: 她把头发漂成了金黄色。

bleach.en: The wood had been bleached by the sun.
bleach.zh: 木头已被太阳晒得褪了色。

bleak.en: The company still hopes to find a buyer, but the future looks bleak.
bleak.zh: 公司仍然希望找到买家，但前景渺茫。

bleed.zh: 非常不幸，她失血过多死了。

blend.en: Leave the sauce to allow the flavours to blend together.
blend.zh: 让酱汁放一放，使各种味道调和起来。

blend.en: Blend the sugar, eggs, and flour.
blend.zh: 把糖、鸡蛋和面粉掺在一起。

bless.en: He’s always willing to help. Bless him!
bless.zh: 他一向乐于助人，愿上帝保佑他！

bless.en: We’re both blessed with good health.
bless.zh: 我们俩都有福气，身体很好。

blessing.en: The dishwasher has been a real blessing!
blessing.zh: 这洗碗机真是个好东西！

blessing.en: It’s a blessing no one was badly hurt.

blind.en: She’s almost blind in her right eye.
He was slowly going blind (=becoming blind).

blink.en: I blinked as I came out into the sunlight.
blink.zh: 我走出来，在太阳光下直眨眼睛。

blink.en: The light on your answering machine is blinking.
blink.zh: 你电话答录机上的指示灯在闪。

blip.en: A government spokesman described the rise in inflation as a temporary blip.
blip.zh: 一位政府发言人称通货膨胀率上升只是暂时现象。

bliss.en: I didn’t have to get up till 11 – it was sheer bliss.

blister.en: New shoes always give me blisters.
blister.zh: 我穿新鞋脚上总是起泡。

blister.en: The paint will blister in the heat.

block.en: Head for 44th Street, a few blocks east of Sixth Avenue.
The church is down the block.
block.zh: 教堂就在这个街区那头。

blood.en: Her body was found in a pool of blood.
blood.zh: 她的尸体被发现倒在血泊之中。

blood.en: Blood oozed from a cut on his forehead.
blood.zh: 血从他额头的伤口里渗了出来。

bloodstream.en: The drug is injected directly into the bloodstream.
bloodstream.zh: 这种药物是直接注射到血液中的。

bloom.en: The rosy bloom of her cheeks had faded.
bloom.zh: 她双颊那红润的光泽已经消失。

bloom.en: She was blooming the last time I saw her.
bloom.zh: 我上次见到她的时候她容光焕发。

blossom.en: The cherry tree was covered in blossom.
The apple trees are just beginning to blossom.

blot.en: Thick white smoke blotted out the sun.
blot.zh: 白色的浓烟遮住了太阳。

blot.en: She said she took drugs to blot out her problems.
blot.zh: 她说她吸毒是为了排遣烦恼。

blow.en: A cold breeze was blowing hard.
It was blowing from an easterly direction.

blue.en: I’ve been feeling kind of blue.
You can tell them till you’re blue in the face, but they’ll still do what they want.
blue.zh: 你就算费尽唇舌，他们还是会独断独行。

blueprint.en: By changing the tomato’s genetic blueprint, scientists can alter the rate at which it ripens.
blueprint.zh: 科学家可以通过改变番茄的基因蓝图来改变它的成熟速度。

bluff.en: You wouldn’t really tell her. You’re bluffing!
bluff.zh: 你不会真的告诉她吧，你在吓唬我！

bluff.en: I hope we’ll be able to bluff our way past the guard.
bluff.zh: 我希望我们可以骗过保安。

bluish.en: Her skin had a bluish tinge.
bluish.zh: 她的皮肤微微透着蓝色。

blunder.en: A last-minute blunder cost them the match.
blunder.zh: 最后一刻的失误使他们输掉了这场比赛。

blunder.en: Someone was blundering about in the kitchen.
blunder.zh: 有人在厨房里四处瞎撞。

blunt.zh: 把你所有的钝刀子都磨一磨。

blunt.en: To be blunt, many of the candidates cannot read or write.
blunt.zh: 说得不客气一点，很多申请人都不会读写。

bluntly.en: To put it bluntly, she’s not up to the job.
bluntly.zh: 恕我直言，她不适合这份工作。

blur.en: I saw the blur of the car as it passed in front of me.
blur.zh: 汽车从我面前驶过，我只看到一个模糊的影子。

blur.en: The island was a blur through misty rain.
blur.zh: 小岛在蒙蒙烟雨中影影绰绰。

blush.en: Wilson saw she was watching him and blushed.
blush.zh: 威尔逊看到她在注视着自己，不由得脸红了。

blush.en: Joan blushed at the unexpected compliment.
blush.zh: 这意外的夸奖让琼脸红了。

board.en: The plan of the new building is displayed on a board at the back of the room.
board.zh: 新大楼的设计图贴在房间后面的公告板上。

board.en: I’ve put a list of names up on the board.
board.zh: 我在布告板上贴出了名单。

boarding.en: Boarding is now taking place at Gate 38.

boast.en: Amy boasted that her son was a genius.
boast.zh: 埃米夸耀自己的儿子是天才。

boast.en: He’s boasting about how much money he has made.
boast.zh: 他在吹嘘自己赚了多少多少钱。

boat.en: The boat capsized (=turned over) in heavy seas.
boat.zh: 船在波涛汹涌的大海上倾覆了。

boat.en: Some of the beaches can only be reached by boat.
boat.zh: 有些海滩只有乘船才能抵达。

bob.en: The boat bobbed gently up and down on the water.
bob.zh: 小船在水面上轻轻起伏。

bob.en: Mrs Foster bobbed about, gathering up her things.
bob.zh: 福斯特夫人跑来跑去，收拾自己的东西。

bode.en: The opinion polls do not bode well for the Democrats.
bode.zh: 民意调查的结果对于民主党不是个好兆头。

bodily.en: He lifted the child bodily aboard.
bodily.zh: 他把孩子整个抱起来放到车上。

bodily.en: The column was transferred bodily to a new site by the bank of the river.
bodily.zh: 那根圆柱被整体迁到河堤边的一个新址。

body.en: My fingers were numb and my whole body ached.
Your body temperature is higher in the daytime than at night.
body.zh: 人的体温白天高于夜晚。

bodyguard.en: The senator arrived, surrounded by personal bodyguards.
bodyguard.zh: 这位参议员在私人保镖的簇拥下抵达。

bog.en: Talks to settle the pay dispute have become bogged down.
bog.zh: 解决工资纠纷的会谈陷入了僵局。

bog.en: Don’t let yourself get bogged down in minor details.
bog.zh: 不要让细枝末节的问题拖住。

boil.en: Put the spaghetti into plenty of boiling salted water.
boil.zh: 把意大利面放入大量煮沸的盐水中。

boiling.en: Can I open a window? It’s boiling in here.
boiling.zh: 我开扇窗好吗？这里热死人了。

boiling.en: It was a boiling hot morning.
boiling.zh: 那是一个奇热无比的早晨。

bold.en: In a surprisingly bold move, he is threatening court action against the company.
bold.zh: 他出人意料地做出一个大胆举动，威胁要起诉这家公司。

bold.en: My aunt Flo was a bold determined woman.
bold.zh: 我姑妈芙洛是一个大胆果断的人。

bolster.en: He is making a bold attempt to bolster the territory’s confidence.
bolster.zh: 他正在采取大胆行动以提振辖区信心。

bolt.en: Was this money a bolt from the blue or did you know you were going to get it?
bolt.zh: 这是一笔意料之财呢，还是你本来就知道会有的？

bolt.en: There’s not much left of his house after it was struck by a bolt of lightning.
bolt.zh: 他的房子遭雷击之后差不多全毁了。

bomb.en: The bomb went off at 9.30 in the morning.
Enemy planes dropped over 200 bombs during the raid.
bomb.zh: 袭击中敌机投下了两百多枚炸弹。

bombard.en: I had been in action, bombarding the Normandy coast.
bombard.zh: 我参加过轰炸诺曼底海岸的行动。

bombard.en: The office was bombarded by telephone calls.
bombard.zh: 办公室里电话响个不停。

bombardment.en: The bombardment continued for a terrible nine hours.
bombardment.zh: 轰炸可怕地持续了九个小时。

bona fide.en: Only bona fide members are allowed to use the club pool.
bona fide.zh: 只有真正的会员才允许使用俱乐部的泳池。

bond.en: My father put all his money into stock market bonds.
bond.zh: 我父亲把他所有的钱都投在上市债券上。

bond.en: Use a glue gun to form a strong bond on wood or china.
bond.zh: 用喷胶枪使木头或瓷器牢固地黏合起来。

bondage.en: Since the age of 13, he had been in bondage.

bone.en: The X-ray showed that the bone was broken in two places.

bonus.en: Long-term savers qualify for a cash bonus.
bonus.zh: 长期储户可获现金红利。

bonus.en: Further additions to your pay may take the form of bonus payments.
bonus.zh: 工资以外的钱可能以奖金的形式发放。

bony.en: She had a bony intelligent face.
bony.zh: 她的脸很瘦，看来很聪明。

book.en: I’ve just started reading a book by Graham Greene.
An accountant will examine the company’s books.
book.zh: 一名会计师将给公司查账。

booking.en: I made a booking for two double rooms.
booking.zh: 我预订了两个双人房间。

booking.en: I’m calling to confirm my booking (=say definitely that I want to travel etc).
booking.zh: 我打电话是想确认一下我的预订。

boom.en: The boom has created job opportunities.
boom.zh: 经济繁荣创造了就业的机会。

boom.en: In boom times, airlines do well.
boom.zh: 在经济繁荣时期，航空公司生意很好。

boon.en: The bus service is a real boon to people in the village.
boon.zh: 公共汽车服务对村里的人来说是一大便利之处。

boost.en: The new resort area has boosted tourism.
boost.zh: 新的度假区促进了旅游业的发展。

boost.en: The win boosted the team’s confidence.
boost.zh: 这一场胜利增加了球队的信心。

boot.en: The new model has a bigger boot.
The chairman denied that he had been given the boot.
boot.zh: 主席否认他是被炒鱿鱼的。

border.en: To cross the border, you will need a valid passport.
border.zh: 过边境需要持有效护照。

border.en: He helped them to get across the border.

bore.en: He’s the sort of person who bores you at parties.
bore.zh: 他这人会在派对上烦你。

bore.en: I won’t bore you with all the technical details.
bore.zh: 我不想讲技术上的细节让大家烦。

boring.en: Her husband is about the most boring person I’ve ever met.
boring.zh: 她丈夫可以说是我见过的最无聊的人。

boring.en: The job was dull and boring.

born.en: Forty lambs were born this spring.

borrow.en: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?
borrow.zh: 我可以借你的笔用一下吗？

borrow.en: You are allowed to borrow six books from the library at a time.
borrow.zh: 你每次可从图书馆借六本书。

bosom.en: She cradled the child to her bosom.
Drury harboured bitterness in his bosom.

boss.en: I’ll have to ask my boss for a day off.
Since I’m my own boss (=I work for myself, rather than for an employer), my hours are flexible.
boss.zh: 我自己当老板，所以我的时间很灵活。

bother.en: He didn’t bother to answer the question.
He didn’t bother with a reply.

bottle.en: Between us, we drank three bottles of wine.
bottle.zh: 我们俩喝了三瓶葡萄酒。

bottle.en: My first baby just wouldn’t take a bottle at all.
bottle.zh: 我的第一个孩子根本就不肯用奶瓶喝奶。

bottom.en: Can you hold the bottom of the ladder for me?
bottom.zh: 你帮我扶住梯子底部好吗？

bottom.en: Grandma was standing at the bottom of the stairs.
bottom.zh: 祖母正站在楼梯的下面。

bounce.en: The ball bounced off the post and into the goal.
bounce.zh: 球从门柱上弹入了球门。

bounce.en: The kids were bouncing a ball against the wall.
bounce.zh: 孩子们正在对着墙打球。

bound.en: Don’t lie to her. She’s bound to find out.
bound.zh: 别骗她，她肯定会发现的。

bound.en: When you are dealing with so many patients, mistakes are bound to happen.
bound.zh: 你要照顾这么多病人，失误在所难免。

boundary.en: The Mississippi River forms a natural boundary between Iowa and Illinois.
boundary.zh: 密西西比河是艾奥瓦州和伊利诺伊州的天然边界。

boundary.en: National boundaries are becoming increasingly meaningless in the global economy.
boundary.zh: 在全球经济中，国界已经变得越来越没有意义。

bounty.en: People came from all over the world to enjoy America’s bounty.
bounty.zh: 人们从世界各地而来，享受美国的富足。

bourgeois.en: She came from a bourgeois family.
bourgeois.zh: 她来自一个中产阶级家庭。

bow.en: She bowed and left the stage.
bow.zh: 她鞠了一躬，离开了舞台。

bow.en: Corbett entered the room, bowing respectfully.
bow.zh: 科比特走进房间，恭敬地鞠了一躬。

bowl.en: Mix all the ingredients thoroughly in a large bowl.
bowl.zh: 将所有配料放在大碗里搅拌均匀。

bowling.en: Do you want to go bowling with us Friday?
bowling.zh: 星期五想和我们一起去打保龄球吗？

box.en: Put an ‘X’ in the box if you would like to join our mailing list.
box.zh: 如果你想加入我们的邮寄名单，请在方框内打X

box.en: The box on the left gives a short history of the battle.
box.zh: 左边方框内简要介绍了这场战役的经过。

boy.en: The boys wanted to play football.
A group of teenage boys stood talking in a group outside.
boy.zh: 一群十几岁的男孩站在外面交谈。

boycott.en: We boycott all products tested on animals.
boycott.zh: 我们抵制所有拿动物做试验的产品。

boycott.en: They are now trying to organize a boycott.
boycott.zh: 他们正试图组织一场抵制行动。

brace.en: Nancy braced herself for the inevitable arguments.
brace.zh: 南希为这场无法避免的争论作好了准备。

brace.en: The military needs to brace itself for further spending cuts, says McCoy.
brace.zh: 麦科伊称，军方需要做好再次削减开支的准备。

bracket.en: Last year’s sales figures are given in brackets.
bracket.zh: 去年的销售额放在括弧中。

bracket.en: Women and minors were bracketed together for the legislation.
bracket.zh: 这项法规中妇女和未成年人被归为一类。

brag.en: Ben’s always bragging about his success with women.
brag.zh: 本总是吹嘘他对女人很有办法。

brag.en: Julia used to brag that her family had a villa in Spain.
brag.zh: 朱莉娅以前老吹嘘她家在西班牙有一栋别墅。

brain.en: Messages from the brain are carried by the central nervous system.
brain.zh: 大脑发出的信息是通过中枢神经系统传递的。

brain.en: Emotional responses are a function of the right hemisphere of the brain.
brain.zh: 情绪反应是右脑的一项功能。

brainstorm.en: I must have had a brainstorm that afternoon.
brainstorm.zh: 那天下午我肯定是一时糊涂了。

brake.en: Test your brakes after driving through water.
brake.zh: 车子涉水之后要检验一下刹车。

brake.en: I managed to put the brakes on just in time.

branch.en: After the storm, the ground was littered with twigs and branches.
branch.zh: 暴风雨过后，满地都是大大小小的树枝。

branch.en: The topmost branches were full of birds.

brand.en: What brand of detergent do you use?
brand.zh: 你用什么牌子的洗涤剂？

brand.en: You can’t brand all football supporters as hooligans.
brand.zh: 你不能给所有的足球迷都加上流氓的恶名。

brand-new.zh: 他的衣服看上去是全新的。

brash.en: The painting was bold, brash, and modern.
brash.zh: 这幅画大胆、醒目，而且现代。

brave.en: It was brave of you to speak in front of all those people.
brave.zh: 你很勇敢，能在那么多人面前说话。

brave.en: Today we remember the brave who died in the last war.
brave.zh: 今天我们要纪念在上一场战争中牺牲的勇士。

brawl.zh: 球迷们在体育馆外面闹事。

breach.en: This was a clear breach of the 1994 Trade Agreement.
They sued the company for breach of contract.
breach.zh: 他们起诉这家公司违反合同。

bread.en: Would you like some bread with your soup?
bread.zh: 你喝汤时要吃点面包吗？

bread.en: Writing is my bread and butter.

breadbasket.en: Zambia could be the breadbasket of Africa.
breadbasket.zh: 赞比亚可能成为非洲重要的产粮区。

breadth.en: The boat measured 15 feet in length and 4 feet in breadth.
The job wasn’t giving him the breadth of experience he wanted.
breadth.zh: 这个工作没有让他获得他想要的多方面的经验。

break.en: I had to break a window to get into the house.
break.zh: 我只得打破一扇窗户进屋。

break.en: Don’t lean on the fence like that – you’ll break it!

breakage.en: All breakages must be paid for.

breakdown.en: He moved away after the breakdown of his marriage.
breakdown.zh: 他婚姻破裂以后就搬走了。

breakdown.en: A sudden rise in oil prices could lead to a breakdown of the economy.
breakdown.zh: 油价暴涨会导致经济崩溃。

breakfast.en: We had bacon and eggs for breakfast.
breakfast.zh: 我们早餐吃了熏肉鸡蛋。

breakthrough.en: Scientists have made a major breakthrough in the treatment of cancer.
breakthrough.zh: 科学家在癌症治疗方面取得了重大突破。

breast.en: These bras are specially designed for women with large breasts.
breast.zh: 这些胸罩专为乳房丰满的女性设计。

breast.en: Dick cradled her photograph against his breast.
breast.zh: 迪克把她的照片轻轻拥在胸前。

breath.en: Leo could smell the wine on her breath.
breath.zh: 利奥闻到她呼吸中有葡萄酒的味道。

breathe.en: The room filled with smoke, and it was becoming difficult to breathe.
breathe.zh: 房间里全是烟，呼吸越来越困难。

breathe.en: People are concerned about the quality of the air they breathe.
breathe.zh: 人们关心他们所呼吸的空气的质量。

breathless.en: The long climb left Jan feeling breathless.
breathless.zh: 攀爬了那么长时间，简感到喘不过气来。

breathtaking.en: The view from my bedroom window was absolutely breathtaking.
breathtaking.zh: 我卧室窗外的景色美得令人窒息。

breed.en: Eagles breed during the cooler months of the year.
breed.zh: 鹰在一年中较凉爽的季节交配繁殖。

breed.en: These dogs were originally bred in Scotland to round up sheep.
breed.zh: 这些狗最初在苏格兰是为了圈羊而饲养的。

breeze.en: Don’t think that learning Dutch will be a breeze.
breeze.zh: 不要以为学荷兰语是件轻松的事。

brew.en: Every beer on the menu was brewed locally.
brew.zh: 酒单上的所有啤酒都是本地酿造的。

brew.en: He read the paper while the tea brewed.
brew.zh: 他趁泡茶的时候读报纸。

bribe.en: The only way we could get into the country was by bribing the border officials.
bribe.zh: 我们要进入这个国家，唯一的办法是贿赂边境官员。

bribe.en: He bribed one of the guards to smuggle out a note.
bribe.zh: 他买通其中的一个警卫，让他偷偷地带一张字条出去。

bribery.en: We tried everything – persuasion, bribery, threats.
He was found guilty of bribery and corruption (=bribery and dishonest behaviour).
bribery.zh: 他被判犯有贿赂和徇私舞弊罪。

brick.en: Protesters attacked the police with stones and bricks.
brick.zh: 抗议者用石头和砖块袭击警察。

brick.en: Some of the rooms had been bricked off.
brick.zh: 有几间房是用砖墙隔出来的。

bridge.en: The training programme is seen as a bridge between school and work.
bridge.zh: 该培训计划被视为衔接学校和职场的桥梁。

bridge.en: The differences between our two cultures can be bridged if we continue to communicate.
bridge.zh: 如果保持沟通，我们两种文化之间的分歧可以消除。

bridle.en: The senator bridled at the reporter’s question.
bridle.zh: 记者的问题惹怒了参议员。

brief.en: We stopped by Alice’s house for a brief visit.
brief.zh: 我们顺路在艾丽斯家小坐片刻。

brief.en: Let’s keep this conversation brief; I have a plane to catch.
brief.zh: 我们长话短说吧，我还要赶飞机。

briefly.en: We stopped off briefly in London.
Sonia explained briefly what we had to do.
briefly.zh: 索尼娅简要地说明了我们要做的事。

bright.en: Her eyes were hurting from the bright lights.
bright.zh: 明亮的光线刺痛了她的眼睛。

bright.en: The weather was bright and sunny.

brighten.en: Use blonde highlights to brighten your hair.
brighten.zh: 用点金色的挑染，让你的发色明亮起来。

brighten.en: The morning sunshine brightened up the room.
brighten.zh: 清晨的阳光照亮了房间。

brilliance.en: He is also respected for his brilliance as an artist.
brilliance.zh: 他的艺术才华同样被人尊敬。

brilliance.en: The stars glittered with the brilliance of jewels.
brilliance.zh: 群星闪耀，犹如一颗颗璀璨的宝石。

brilliant.en: She closed her eyes against the brilliant light.
brilliant.zh: 强烈的光线下，她闭起了眼睛。

brilliant.en: We sat outside in the brilliant sunshine.
brilliant.zh: 我们坐在外面，沐浴在灿烂的阳光下。

brim.en: She filled each glass to the brim.
brim.zh: 她把每个杯子都斟得满满的。

brim.en: The cup was filled to the brim with coffee.
brim.zh: 杯子里倒了满满的一杯咖啡。

bring.en: It was the first time Joey had ever brought a girl home.
bring.zh: 那是乔伊第一次带女孩子回家。

brink.en: In October 1962 the world seemed on the brink of nuclear war.
The company had huge debts and was on the brink of collapse.
brink.zh: 公司背负巨额债务，已濒临破产。

brisk.en: They set off at a brisk pace.
brisk.zh: 他们踏着轻快的步伐上路了。

brisk.en: Her tone of voice is brisk.

bristle.en: His chin was covered with bristles.
John pushed back his chair, bristling with rage.
bristle.zh: 约翰把椅子往后一推，暴跳起来。

brittle.en: The branches were dry and brittle.
Joanna was diagnosed as having brittle bones.
brittle.zh: 乔安娜被诊断为骨质疏松。

broad.en: We went along a broad passage.
broad.zh: 我们走在一条宽阔的走廊上。

broad.en: He was six feet tall, with broad shoulders.
broad.zh: 他身高六英尺，肩膀宽阔。

broadcast.en: CNN’s live broadcast of the trial (=sent out at the same time as the events are happening)
broadcast.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网对这场庭审的现场直播

broadcast.en: The interview was broadcast live across Europe.
broadcast.zh: 这次采访向整个欧洲进行了现场直播。

broaden.en: The course helps school-leavers broaden their knowledge of the world of work.
broaden.zh: 这门课程有助于毕业生增加对职场的了解。

broaden.en: I’d like to work abroad to broaden my horizons (=learn, experience, or attempt new things).
broaden.zh: 我想去国外工作，开阔眼界。

broadly.en: She knows broadly what to expect.
broadly.zh: 她大致知道会有什么结果。
我们得出了大致相同的结论。

broadside.en: Can the government survive this latest broadside from its own supporters?
broadside.zh: 政府能否顶住其支持者最近的猛烈抨击？

broadside.en: I brought the boat in broadside to the beach.

broke.en: I’m fed up with being broke all the time.
broke.zh: 我受够了老是身无分文。

broke.en: A lot of small businesses went broke in the recession.
broke.zh: 经济衰退的时候许多小企业都破产了。

broken.en: Do you know how the phone got broken (=became broken)?
broken.zh: 你知道电话是怎么坏掉的吗？

bronze.en: King won a bronze in the 100-metres.

brood.en: Don’t sit at home brooding all day.
brood.zh: 别整天坐在家里闷闷不乐的。

brood.en: There’s no point brooding over it – she’s gone.
brood.zh: 老是想这件事也没用，她都已经走了。

brook.en: He would brook no criticism, even from his beloved daughter.
brook.zh: 他不能容忍任何批评，哪怕是自己深爱的女儿也不行。

brother.en: I have two brothers, William and Mark.
brother.zh: 我有两个兄弟，威廉和马克。

brother.en: My younger brother is a doctor.

brow.en: His brow furrowed. ‘I don’t understand, ’ he said.

brown.en: He’d been on vacation and looked very brown.
brown.zh: 他去度了假，看上去晒得很黑。

brown.en: He was as brown as a berry after two weeks in the sun.
brown.zh: 他晒了两个星期的太阳，皮肤变得黝黑黝黑的。

browse.en: Jon was browsing through the photographs.
The trip allows you plenty of time for browsing around the shops.
browse.zh: 此次旅行会让你有足够的时间逛商店。

bruise.en: She fell off her bike and bruised her knee.
bruise.zh: 她从自行车上摔下来，擦伤了膝盖。

bruise.en: The incident had bruised his pride.
bruise.zh: 这件事挫伤了他的自尊心。

brush.en: I’ll just give my hair a quick brush.
His first brush with the law came when he was 16.
brush.zh: 他第一次差点犯法是在他16

brute.en: Discussion can be more effective than the use of brute force.
The brute fact is that the situation will not improve.
brute.zh: 情况不会好转，这是赤裸裸的事实。

bubble.en: When water boils, bubbles rise to the surface.
bubble.zh: 水烧开时，水面会冒泡泡。

bubble.en: She was blowing bubbles in her milk with a straw.
bubble.zh: 她用吸管在牛奶里吹泡泡。

bubbly.en: She has a very bubbly personality.

buck.en: The movie is about a group of men trying to make a buck (=earn some money) as male strippers.
buck.zh: 这部影片讲的是一群男人想通过跳脱衣舞赚钱的故事。

bucket.en: They were drinking beer by the bucket.
They made buckets of cash on the deal.
bucket.zh: 这笔生意他们赚大发了。

buckle.en: The steel pillars began to buckle.
The rails buckled under the intense heat of the fire.
buckle.zh: 铁轨在烈火的高温下变了形。

budget.en: The budget for photography has been cut.
budget.zh: 摄影方面的预算被削减了。

budget.en: We had a really tight budget.

buffer.en: Eastern Europe was important to Russia as a buffer against the West.
buffer.zh: 东欧是俄罗斯与西方抗衡的重要缓冲。

buffer.en: She often had to act as a buffer between father and son.
buffer.zh: 她经常要充当父子之间的调解人。

buffet.en: The price includes morning coffee, buffet lunch, and afternoon tea.
buffet.zh: 这一价格包含早晨的咖啡、自助午餐和下午茶。

buffet.en: London was buffeted by storms last night.
buffet.zh: 伦敦昨晚遭到暴风雨的袭击。

bug.en: I picked up a bug last weekend.
bug.zh: 上个周末我生了一场小病。

bug.en: There’s a nasty bug going round (=that a lot of people have caught).
bug.zh: 现在流行着一种很烦人的传染病。

bugbear.zh: 文书工作是我们最头痛的事。

build.en: The purpose is to build new houses for local people.
build.zh: 目的是要为当地居民建造新的住宅。

build.en: The road took many years to build.

building.en: The offices are on the top two floors of the building.
building.zh: 办公室在大楼最高的两层。

building.en: There is a limited supply of land for building.

built-up.en: He was fined for speeding in a built-up area.
built-up.zh: 他因为在建筑物密集的地区超速行驶而被罚款。

bulge.en: The gun made a bulge under his jacket.
bulge.zh: 手枪从他的夹克里面鼓了出来。

bulge.en: His pockets were bulging with candy.
bulge.zh: 他的口袋里鼓鼓囊囊塞满了糖果。

bulk.en: The bulk of consumers are based in towns.
bulk.zh: 大多数消费者都是城镇居民。

bulk.en: The dough will rise until it is double in bulk.
bulk.zh: 面团会发酵到原来的两倍大。

bull.en: Nora decided to take the bull by the horns and organize things for herself.
bull.zh: 诺拉决定迎难而上，自己来安排事情。

bullet.en: He was killed by a single bullet.
Several bullet holes could be seen beside a window.
bullet.zh: 窗户边可以看到几个弹孔。

bullish.en: He’s very bullish about the company’s prospects.
bullish.zh: 他对公司的前景充满信心。

bully.zh: 恃强凌弱者往往是懦夫。

bully.en: Don’t let them bully you into working on Saturdays.
bully.zh: 不要让他们逼你星期六上班。

bump.en: I ran after him, bumping against people in my hurry.
bump.zh: 我在后面追他，匆忙间撞到了别人身上。

bump.en: Tim was a clumsy boy, always bumping into the furniture.
bump.zh: 蒂姆是个笨手笨脚的孩子，老是撞到家具上。

bumper.en: We hope readers will enjoy this bumper issue of ‘Homes and Gardens’.
bumper.zh: 我们希望读者会喜欢这一期特大号的《家园》。

bumpy.en: The ground is bumpy in places.
bumpy.zh: 地上有些地方高低不平。

bumpy.en: The plane made a bumpy landing.

bunch.en: I’ll send her a bunch of flowers.
bunch.zh: 我会给她送去一束鲜花。

bunch.en: He had a bunch of keys on his belt.
bunch.zh: 他皮带上挂了一串钥匙。

bundle.en: College evening classes cost a bundle.
bundle.zh: 大学的夜间课程收费很高。

bundle.en: A company can make a bundle by selling unwanted property.
bundle.zh: 公司出售多余资产可以赚一大笔钱。

bunk.en: You can bunk down on the sofa for tonight.
bunk.zh: 今天晚上你可以睡在沙发上。

buoyant.en: Phil was in a buoyant mood.

burden.en: His family responsibilities had started to become a burden.
burden.zh: 家庭责任已开始成为他的负担。

burden.en: The burden of taxation has risen considerably.

censor.en: The information given to the press was carefully censored by the Ministry of Defence.
censor.zh: 发布给报界的信息经过了国防部的仔细审查。

central.en: The roof is supported by a central column.
central.zh: 屋顶由一根中心柱支撑着。

centre.en: There was an enormous oak table in the center of the room.
centre.zh: 房间中央有一张巨大的橡木桌子。

centre.en: The hotel is right in the centre of the village.
centre.zh: 这家旅馆在村子的正中心。

century.en: The church was built in the 13th century.

ceremony.en: The queen was crowned with due ceremony.
ceremony.zh: 女王按照规定的礼仪加冕。

ceremony.en: He wished me good luck in the future and left without further ceremony.
ceremony.zh: 他祝愿我将来交到好运，然后就不客气地走了。

certain.en: I’m absolutely certain that I left the keys in the kitchen.
certain.zh: 我绝对肯定我把钥匙落在厨房里了。

certain.en: I felt certain that I’d passed the test.
certain.zh: 我感觉自己肯定通过这次测验了。

certainly.en: I certainly never expected to become a writer.
certainly.zh: 我当然从未期望自己成为一名作家。
这些东西肯定不是我的。

certainty.en: She knew with absolute certainty that he’d say no.
The result is impossible to predict with any degree of certainty.
certainty.zh: 这一结果完全无法确切预测。

certification.en: We successfully completed the certification for open water diving.
certification.zh: 我们成功地拿到了开放水域潜水证书。

certify.en: The accounts were certified by an auditor.
certify.zh: 这些账目经审计员核实过。

certify.en: We need to certify that the repairs have been satisfactorily carried out.
certify.zh: 我们需要核实修理工作完成得令人满意。

chafe.en: Wear a T-shirt under your wet suit to stop it chafing.
Some hunters are chafing under the new restrictions.
chafe.zh: 一些猎人对这些新的限制规定感到十分恼怒。

chain.en: She had a gold chain around her neck.
chain.zh: 她脖子上戴了条金项链。

chain.en: The salesmen are just one link in the chain (=part of a process) of distribution.
chain.zh: 销售员只是整个经销过程中的一个环节。

chair.en: They bought a new table and chairs.
chair.zh: 他们买了一套新的桌椅。

chair.en: One of the chair legs was broken.

chairman.en: Potts was appointed chairman of the education committee.
chairman.zh: 波茨被任命为教育委员会主席。
巴雷特担任副主席一职。

chalk.en: The two brothers are as different as chalk and cheese.
They’re like chalk and cheese, those two.

chalky.en: There were chalky bits in the bottom of the drink.
chalky.zh: 饮料底层有粉笔灰一样的东西。

challenge.en: The company is ready to meet the challenges of the next few years.
challenge.zh: 公司已准备好迎接今后几年的挑战。

challenge.en: I relish the challenge of rebuilding the club.
challenge.zh: 我从重建俱乐部的挑战中获得乐趣。

challenging.en: Teaching young children is a challenging and rewarding job.
challenging.zh: 幼儿教育是一项具有挑战性和有意义的工作。

championship.zh: 希腊队赢得了欧洲锦标赛的冠军。

championship.en: Warwickshire are the current holders of the cricket championship.
championship.zh: 沃里克郡队是板球的现任冠军。

chance.en: There’s always the chance that something will go wrong.
What are the team’s chances of success?
chance.zh: 球队获胜的希望有多大？

chancellor.en: Helmut Kohl, the former German Chancellor

change.en: Susan has changed a lot since I last saw her.
change.zh: 自从我上次见到苏珊之后，她变了许多。

change.en: Changing your eating habits is the best way to lose weight.
change.zh: 改变饮食习惯是减肥的最佳方法。

channel.en: The kids are watching cartoons on the Disney Channel.
channel.zh: 孩子们在看迪士尼频道的卡通片。

chant.en: Others in the crowd took up the chant (=began chanting).
chant.zh: 人群中的其他人开始一遍遍呼喊起来。

chaos.en: The country was plunged into economic chaos.
chaos.zh: 这个国家陷入了经济大混乱。

chaos.en: There was total chaos on the roads.

chapel.en: Bethan goes to chapel every Sunday.
chapel.zh: 贝唐每个星期天都去教堂做礼拜。

chapter.en: This chapter discusses power, and how people use it.
chapter.zh: 这一章节讲权力，以及人们如何运用权力。

char.en: Roast the peppers until the skin begins to char and blister.
char.zh: 把这些辣椒烤到表皮发黑起泡为止。

character.en: He has a cheerful but quiet character.
Children grow up with a mixture of character traits (=character qualities) from both sides of their family.
character.zh: 儿童在成长过程中会把父母亲双方的性格特点都继承下来。

characteristic.en: Violent images are a defining characteristic of his work.
characteristic.zh: 暴力形象是他作品的一个鲜明特征。

characterization.en: Pilcher’s books have humour, good characterization, and lively dialogue.
characterization.zh: 皮尔彻的书风趣幽默，人物塑造到位，而且对话生动。

characterize.en: The group was characterized as being well-educated and liberal.
characterize.zh: 该群体被描绘成受过良好教育，思想开明。
明亮的色彩是他绘画作品的特点。

charge.en: There is a charge for the use of the swimming pool.
Guided tours are provided at no charge.
charge.zh: 免费提供有导游带队的观光游览。

charity.en: Several charities sent aid to the flood victims.
charity.zh: 有几家慈善机构已向洪灾灾民送去了救援物资。

charity.en: All the money raised by the concert will go to charity.
charity.zh: 音乐会筹得的钱款将全部用于慈善事业。

charm.en: She turned on the charm (=used her charm) to all the men.
charm.zh: 她对所有那些男人都施展魅力。

charm.en: The room had no windows and all the charm of a prison cell (=used to say that something has no charm).
charm.zh: 这房间没有窗，简直就是牢房。

charming.zh: 哈里有时候很讨人喜欢。

chart.en: Her new single went straight to number one in the pop charts.
chart.zh: 她新推出的单曲唱片跃居流行歌曲排行榜第一位。

chart.en: Brooks again topped the charts (=was the most popular).
chart.zh: 布鲁克斯再次高居排行榜首位。

charter.en: The town’s charter was granted in 1838.
Reducing the number of police is just a thieves’ charter.
charter.zh: 减少警力等于是给窃贼开了通行证。

chary.en: Banks were chary of lending the company more money.
chary.zh: 银行不愿冒风险贷更多的钱给这家公司。

chase.en: The dogs saw him running and chased him.
chase.zh: 那些狗看到他在跑就追他。

chase.en: The police chased the suspect along Severn Avenue.
chase.zh: 警察沿着塞汶河大街追捕嫌疑犯。

chaste.en: She led a chaste decent life.
chaste.zh: 她过着贞洁正派的生活。

chat.en: John and I sat up until the early hours chatting.
chat.zh: 我和约翰聊到凌晨才睡。

chat.en: Mary was there, chatting to her mother.
chat.zh: 玛丽也在，和她母亲闲聊。

chatter.en: She chattered away happily until she noticed I wasn’t listening.
chatter.zh: 她开心地说个不停，直到发觉我没在听才停下来。

chatter.en: She chattered excitedly like a child.
chatter.zh: 她像个孩子似的兴奋地讲个不停。

cheap.en: Property is cheaper in Spain than here.
cheap.zh: 西班牙的房地产比这里便宜。

cheap.en: The equipment is relatively cheap and simple to use.
cheap.zh: 这种设备相对比较便宜，而且操作简单。

cheapen.en: The good harvest that year cheapened the costs of some raw materials.
cheapen.zh: 那年的好收成使一些原材料的成本有所降低。

cheapen.en: She never compromised or cheapened herself.
cheapen.zh: 她从不妥协，也不会自降身份。

cheat.en: He had cheated in the test by using a calculator.
cheat.zh: 他在考试时作弊，用了计算器。

cheat.en: Don’t look at my cards – that’s cheating.

check.en: Check the tiles carefully before you buy them.
check.zh: 购买之前要把瓷砖仔细检查一下。

check.en: A first rule in solving any mystery is to check the facts.
check.zh: 揭开谜团的第一条规则是核查事实。

checkup.en: It’s important to have regular checkups.
checkup.zh: 定期做体检是很重要的。

cheek.en: Lucy stretched up to kiss his cheek.
cheek.zh: 露西伸长了脖子去亲吻他的脸颊。

cheek.en: Billy had rosy cheeks and blue eyes.
cheek.zh: 比利脸颊红润，长着一双蓝眼睛。

cheeky.en: You did that on purpose, you cheeky little devil!
cheeky.zh: 你是故意那么做的，你这无耻的小混蛋！

cheeky.en: Now don’t be cheeky to your elders, young woman.

cheer.en: A great cheer went up from the crowd.
cheer.zh: 人群中爆发出巨大的欢呼声。

cheer.en: So let’s give a cheer to the kids who passed their exams.
cheer.zh: 那么我们为通过考试的孩子们欢呼吧。

cheerful.en: I’m making a real effort to be cheerful despite everything.
cheerful.zh: 尽管发生了这些事，我还是非常努力让自己保持愉快。

cheerless.en: This is a cold cheerless place.
cheerless.zh: 这是个寒冷、阴郁的地方。

cheerless.en: The day was grey and cheerless.

chemistry.en: It’s obvious that there’s a very real chemistry between them.
chemistry.zh: 很明显他们之间真的非常来电。

cheque.en: They sent me a cheque for £100.

cherish.en: I cherish the memory of that day.

chess.en: They meet fairly often to play chess.
chess.zh: 他们经常在一起下国际象棋。

chest.en: Her heart was pounding in her chest.
chest.zh: 她的心在胸口怦怦直跳。

chest.en: He collapsed with severe chest pains.

chew.en: This meat’s so tough I can hardly chew it!
chew.zh: 这肉太老了，我几乎嚼不动！

chew.en: We gave the dog an old shoe to chew on.
chew.zh: 我们扔了一只旧鞋给狗去啃。

chic.en: Margaret was looking very chic in blue.
chic.zh: 玛格丽特穿着蓝色的衣服看上去很优雅。

chief.en: He was recently appointed chief economist at the Bank of Scotland.
chief.zh: 他最近被任命为苏格兰银行的首席经济学家。

chief.en: One of the chief causes of crime today is drugs.
chief.zh: 毒品是如今犯罪的主要诱因之一。

chiefly.en: The work consists chiefly of interviewing the public.
chiefly.zh: 这份工作主要是采访公众。

chiefly.en: I lived abroad for years, chiefly in Italy.
chiefly.zh: 我在国外生活了很多年，主要在意大利。

child.en: The hotel is ideal for families with young children.
child.zh: 这家宾馆对带小孩的家庭再合适不过。

child.en: The film is not suitable for children under 12.

childhood.en: I had a very happy childhood.

childhood.zh: 大多数传染病发生在儿童时期。

childish.en: I wish politicians would stop this childish name-calling.
childish.zh: 我希望政客们能停止这种幼稚的谩骂。

childless.en: It was a happy but childless marriage.
childless.zh: 这是一桩幸福的婚姻，就是没有孩子。

childlike.en: The sight filled her with childlike excitement.
childlike.zh: 这情景令她像孩子般兴奋起来。
她站着的话，看起来就不那么像小孩子了。

chill.en: There was a slight chill in the air.
Suddenly aware of the morning chill, she closed the window.
chill.zh: 她突然感觉到清晨的寒意，于是关上窗户。

chime.en: The clock in the hall chimed six.
Her views on life didn’t quite chime with mine.
chime.zh: 她的人生观和我的不完全一样。

chimney.en: We can’t light a fire because the chimney hasn’t been swept.
chimney.zh: 烟囱管没有清扫过，我们生不了火。

chin.zh: 他若有所思地抚摸着下巴。

chin.en: Chin up! It’ll be over soon.
chin.zh: 振作点！很快就会过去的。

china.en: I’ll get my best china out.
china.zh: 我要把我最好的瓷器拿出来。

chinese.en: Do you fancy going out for a Chinese?
chinese.zh: 你想不想出去吃顿中餐？

chip.en: Wood chips covered the floor of the workshop.
chip.zh: 工场的地板上满是木屑。

chip.en: There’s a chip in this bowl.

chisel.en: Martin chiselled a hole in the door for the new lock.
chisel.zh: 马丁在门上凿了一个洞装新锁。

chocolate.en: I prefer milk chocolate to dark chocolate.
chocolate.zh: 和黑巧克力比起来，我更喜欢牛奶巧克力。

choice.en: Voters have a choice between three main political parties.
choice.zh: 选民可以在三大政党之间作选择。

choice.en: You have a choice of hotel or self-catering accommodation.
choice.zh: 你可以选择住宾馆或找自理膳食的住宿处。

choir.en: He joined a church choir at the age of eight.
choir.zh: 他八岁时加入了一个教堂唱诗班。

choke.en: He choked on a piece of bread.
Six people choked to death on the fumes.

chomp.en: She was chomping on a bread roll.
British people chomp their way through more than a billion bars of chocolate every year.
chomp.zh: 英国人每年吃掉十亿多条巧克力。

choose.en: It took us ages to choose a new carpet.
choose.zh: 我们挑选新地毯花了很长时间。

choose.en: A panel of judges will choose the winner.
choose.zh: 会由一个评判小组选出冠军。

chop.en: He went outside to chop some more wood for the fire.
chop.zh: 他出去再砍些木材来生火。

chop.en: Can you chop up some carrots for me?
chop.zh: 你能帮我切一些胡萝卜吗？

choppy.en: The small boat bobbed about on the choppy water.
choppy.zh: 小船在波浪起伏的水面上颠簸。

chord.en: Many of the things she says will strike a chord with other young women.
chord.zh: 她说的许多话都能引起其他年轻女子的共鸣。

chord.en: He knew that what he was saying had touched a chord.
chord.zh: 他知道自己说的那番话引起了共鸣。

chore.en: I find driving a real chore.
chore.zh: 我觉得开车是一件很讨厌的事情。

chorus.zh: 唱到副歌时，每个人都跟着齐唱起来。

chorus.en: I sing with the university chorus.
chorus.zh: 我在大学合唱队里唱歌。

christian.en: That wasn’t a very christian thing to do!

christmas.zh: 我们在圣诞节和你见面。

christmas.en: I’ll be in Scotland over Christmas.
christmas.zh: 圣诞节期间我将会在苏格兰。

chronic.en: There is a chronic shortage of teachers.
chronic.zh: 长期存在师资短缺的问题。

chronic.en: He was a chronic alcoholic and unable to hold down a job.
chronic.zh: 他长期酗酒，任何工作都做不久。

chronicle.en: His life is chronicled in a new biography published last week.
chronicle.zh: 他的生平被写成一本新传记，于上周出版。

chronicle.en: The book chronicles the events leading up to the war.
chronicle.zh: 该书记述了导致战争爆发的一系列事件。

chronological.en: We arranged the documents in chronological order.
chronological.zh: 我们把这些文件按时序排列。
这些画按年代顺序陈列。

chronology.en: It is important to establish the chronology of the events.
chronology.zh: 确定这些事件的先后顺序很重要。

chronology.en: The book includes a chronology of his life and works.
chronology.zh: 本书附有他的生平和著作年表。

chug.en: The boat chugged out of the harbour.
The economy just keeps chugging along.
chug.zh: 经济在缓慢而稳步地发展。

chunk.en: The rent takes a large chunk out of my monthly salary.
chunk.zh: 房租占去我月薪的一大部分。

chunk.en: A huge chunk of the audience got up and left before the end of the show.
chunk.zh: 演出还没结束，一大批观众就起身离场了。

church.en: Mrs Dobson invited us to dinner after church.
church.zh: 多布森太太邀请我们做完礼拜后吃饭。

church.en: My parents go to church every Sunday.
church.zh: 我父母每个星期天都去做礼拜。

churn.en: My stomach was churning on the day of the exam.
churn.zh: 考试那天我胃里直翻腾。
我们看着大海波浪翻滚。

cinema.en: It’s on at the local cinema.
cinema.zh: 此片正在当地影院上映。

cinema.en: We decided to go to the cinema.
cinema.zh: 我们决定去电影院看电影。

circle.en: Draw a circle 10 cm in diameter.

circuit.en: We did a circuit of the old city.
circuit.zh: 我们绕着老城走了一圈。

circulate.en: Swimming helps to get the blood circulating through the muscles.
circulate.zh: 游泳有助于肌肉的血液循环。

circulate.en: Ceiling fans circulated warm air around the room.
circulate.zh: 吊扇使暖空气在房间里循环。

circulation.en: Doctors had to remove her leg because of bad circulation.
circulation.zh: 她的一条腿血液循环不畅，医生只得将其切除。

circumference.en: The island is only nine miles in circumference.
circumference.zh: 这座岛屿的环岛周长只有九英里。

circumscribe.en: The president’s power is circumscribed by Congress and the Supreme Court.
circumscribe.zh: 总统的权力受到国会和最高法院的制约。

circumstance.en: The Soviet Union had been forced by circumstances to sign a pact with Nazi Germany.
circumstance.zh: 苏联为形势所迫同纳粹德国签订了一项条约。

circumstance.en: I can’t imagine a circumstance in which I would be willing to steal.
circumstance.zh: 我无法想象我在什么情况下会愿意去偷东西。

circumvent.en: The company opened an account abroad, in order to circumvent the tax laws.
circumvent.zh: 为规避税法，这家公司在国外开设了账户。

circumvent.en: We went north in order to circumvent the mountains.
circumvent.zh: 我们往北走以绕开这些山。

circus.en: The first day of school is always such a circus.
circus.zh: 开学第一天总是这样闹哄哄的。

circus.en: The trial has turned into a media circus.
circus.zh: 这场审判变成了一次乱哄哄的媒体聚会。

citation.en: Turner was issued a traffic citation for reckless driving.
citation.zh: 特纳因鲁莽驾驶收到了交通违章罚单。

citation.en: The essay begins with a citation from ‘Hamlet’.
citation.zh: 这篇文章开头引用了《哈姆雷特》中的一句话。

cite.en: The judge cited a 1956 Supreme Court ruling in her decision.
cite.zh: 法官在她的判决中引用了1956

cite.en: Several factors have been cited as the cause of the unrest.
cite.zh: 好几个因素被引证为这次动乱的起因。

citizen.en: We need our schools to teach students to be good citizens.
citizen.zh: 我们需要学校把学生培养为好公民。

citizen.en: The mayor urged citizens to begin preparing for a major storm.
citizen.zh: 一场特大暴风雨即将到来，市长敦促市民做好准备。

citizenship.en: I have applied for French citizenship.
citizenship.zh: 我已经申请了法国国籍。

citizenship.en: McGuirk holds dual citizenship (=the legal right of being a citizen in two countries) in Ireland and the US.
citizenship.zh: 麦吉尔克拥有爱尔兰和美国的双重国籍。

city.en: The nearest big city was St. Louis.
city.zh: 最近的大城市是圣路易斯。

city.en: The city of Cleveland celebrated its 200th birthday with fireworks and an outdoor concert.
city.zh: 克利夫兰市燃放烟火并举办了一场室外音乐会，庆祝该市成立200

civic.en: Jackson spent the day meeting with local religious and civic leaders.
civic.zh: 杰克逊那天与当地的宗教领袖和市领导会面。

civic.en: It is your civic duty to vote in the local elections.
civic.zh: 在地方选举中投票是公民的义务。

civil.en: They were married in a civil ceremony in May.
civil.zh: 他们在五月份举行了世俗婚礼。

civil.en: Many civil cases can be settled out of court.
civil.zh: 许多民事案件可以庭外和解。

civilian.en: Many innocent civilians were killed during the war.
civilian.zh: 许多无辜的平民在战争中丧生。

civilian.en: It was difficult to return to civilian life after ten years in the military.
civilian.zh: 从军十年后重新过平民生活不容易。

civility.en: Please have the civility to knock before you enter next time.
civility.zh: 下次你进来之前要有点礼貌——

civility.en: We exchanged civilities when we were neighbours, but nothing more.
civility.zh: 我们以前做邻居的时候最多也只是客气地打个招呼。

civilization.en: The book explores the relationship between religion and civilization.
civilization.zh: 本书探讨了宗教和文明的关系。

civilization.en: After a week in the mountains, all I wanted to do was get back to civilization.
civilization.zh: 在山里待了一个星期，我唯一想做的就是回到文明社会中。

civilize.en: The missionaries went out to civilize other places.
civilize.zh: 传教士们去异国他乡教化当地人民。

civilize.en: Ellis was credited with civilizing the Texas prison system.
civilize.zh: 据信是埃利斯改良了得克萨斯州的监狱制度。

claim.en: The product claims that it can make you thin without dieting.
claim.zh: 该产品声称不节食也可让你瘦下来。

claim.en: No responsible therapist will claim to cure your insomnia.
claim.zh: 任何一位负责任的治疗专家都不会断言可以治好你的失眠症。
