simultaneous.zh: 他们俩同时惊慌起来，相互抓住对方的手。

simultaneous.en: Up to twenty users can have simultaneous access to the system.

sin.en: She needed to confess her sins and ask for forgiveness.
sin.zh: 她需要忏悔罪过，请求宽恕。

sin.en: He knew that he had committed a terrible sin.
sin.zh: 他知道自己犯下了可怕的罪行。

since.en: We’ve been waiting here since two o’clock.
since.zh: 我们从两点钟开始就在这里等了。

since.en: I haven’t played rugby since I left university.
since.zh: 我大学毕业后就没打过橄榄球。

sincere.en: I would like to say a sincere thank you to everyone who has helped and supported me.
sincere.zh: 我要对所有帮助和支持过我的人表示由衷的感谢。

sincerely.en: I sincerely hope I’ll see her again.
We are sincerely grateful for your help.
sincerely.zh: 我们由衷地感谢你的帮助。

sincerity.en: I don’t doubt her sincerity, but I think she’s got her facts wrong.
sincerity.zh: 我不怀疑她的诚意，但我认为她没弄清楚事实。

sincerity.en: May I say in all sincerity that we could not have achieved this much without your help and support.
sincerity.zh: 请允许我真心诚意地说:

sinful.en: Dancing was believed to be sinful.
sinful.zh: 跳舞曾被认为是不道德的。

sing.zh: 大多数孩子都喜欢唱歌。

singer.en: Tina Turner’s backing singers (=people who sing with her)

single.en: A single tree gave shade from the sun.
They won the game by a single point.
single.zh: 他们仅以一分的优势赢得比赛。

singly.en: Plant the trees singly or in small groups.
singly.zh: 把这些树单棵或成小片种植。

singular.en: If the subject is singular, use a singular verb.
singular.zh: 如果主语是单数，就用单数动词。

singular.en: He showed a singular lack of tact in the way he handled the situation.
singular.zh: 他处理这局面的方式显得极不得体。

singularity.en: He had an attractive singularity of viewpoint.

sink.en: Their motorboat struck a rock and began to sink.
sink.zh: 他们的摩托艇触了礁，开始下沉。

sink.en: The kids watched as the coin sank to the bottom of the pool.
sink.zh: 孩子们看着那枚硬币沉到池底。

sinuous.en: They followed the sinuous trail deep into the mountains.
sinuous.zh: 他们沿着弯弯曲曲的小径进入深山。

sip.en: She was sitting at the table sipping her coffee.
He sipped at his wine with pleasure.

siren.en: I heard police sirens in the distance.
siren.zh: 我听到了远处的警笛声。

sister.zh: 珍妮特和阿比是两姐妹。

sister.en: He has two sisters and a brother.
sister.zh: 他有两个姊妹和一个弟弟。

sit.en: I sat on the shore and looked at the sea.
She was sitting in a chair by the fire.
sit.zh: 她坐在炉火边的椅子上。

site.en: The house is built on the site of a medieval prison.
site.zh: 这幢房子建在一座中世纪监狱的遗址上。

site.en: He managed to get himself a job on a building site.
site.zh: 他好不容易在建筑工地上找了一份工作。

sitting.en: School dinners are served in three sittings.
I sat down and read the whole book in one sitting.
sitting.zh: 我坐下来，一口气看完了这本书。

situate.en: The women have the opportunity to situate their own struggles in a wider historical context.
situate.zh: 这些女性有机会把她们的斗争和更宽广的历史背景联系起来。

situated.en: The house is situated near the college.
situated.zh: 这幢房子位于学院附近。

situated.en: The hotel is ideally situated near the seafront.
situated.zh: 酒店的位置理想，靠近海滨。

situation.en: I explained the situation to everyone.
situation.zh: 我向大家介绍了一下情况。

situation.en: She coped well in a very difficult situation.

six.en: She arrived just after six (=six o'clock).
He learnt to play the violin when he was six (=six years old).

sixteen.en: He moved to London when he was sixteen (=16 years old).
Let’s have dinner on the 16th (=the 16th day of the month).

sixth.en: Let’s have dinner on the sixth (=the sixth day of the month).
About one sixth of the children admitted to taking drugs.
sixth.zh: 大约六分之一的儿童承认吸毒。

sixty.en: The book was written in the sixties.
I’d say she was in her late sixties.

size.en: He’s a small boy, about John’s size.
size.zh: 他是个小男孩，个子和约翰差不多。

size.en: The Jensens’ house is about the same size as ours.
size.zh: 詹森的房子和我们的差不多大。

skate.en: Put your skates on, or you’ll be late for school.
skate.zh: 动作快点，不然你上学要迟到了。

skate.en: The children skated on the frozen pond.
skate.zh: 孩子们在结冰的池塘上滑冰。

skating.en: We went skating in Central Park.
skating.zh: 我们去中央公园溜冰了。

skeletal.en: Police discovered the skeletal remains of a corpse buried near the river.
skeletal.zh: 警方发现了埋在河边的一具尸骨。

skeleton.en: We agreed on a skeleton outline of the proposal.
skeleton.zh: 我们给提案商定了一个基本框架。

skeleton.en: The disease had reduced Harry to a skeleton.
skeleton.zh: 这场病后，哈里瘦得只剩皮包骨了。

sketch.en: Cantor drew a rough sketch of his apartment on a napkin.
sketch.zh: 坎托在餐巾上画了一幅他公寓的草图。

sketch.en: Her TV programme is made up of a series of comic sketches.
sketch.zh: 她的电视节目由一系列滑稽短剧组成。

sketchy.en: Details of the accident are still sketchy.
sketchy.zh: 事故的详细情况依然不完全。

skew.en: All the people we questioned lived in the same area, which had the effect of skewing the figures.
skew.zh: 我们询问的人全都生活在同一地区，这影响了数据的准确性。

skew.en: These assumptions about Communism skewed American foreign policy for decades.
skew.zh: 对于共产主义的这些臆断使美国外交政策数十年来有失偏颇。

ski.en: We skied down to the village of Argentière.
ski.zh: 我们滑雪下坡，到了阿让蒂耶尔村。

skiing.en: We’re going to go skiing in Colorado this winter.
skiing.zh: 今年冬天我们要去科罗拉多滑雪。

skilful.en: After a few years, he became very skilful at drawing.
skilful.zh: 几年以后，他的绘画技艺已经非常纯熟了。

skilful.en: She had used make-up skilfully to mask the bruise.
skilful.zh: 她用巧妙的化妆把瘀伤遮住了。

skill.en: Reading and writing are two different skills.
skill.zh: 阅读和写作是两种不同的技能。

skill.en: Many jobs today require computer skills.
skill.zh: 如今的许多工作都需要计算机技能。

skilled.en: Skilled craftsmen, such as carpenters, are in great demand.
skilled.zh: 对木工之类的熟练工匠需求量很大。

skilled.en: The company is fortunate to have such highly skilled workers.
skilled.zh: 公司有这样一些技能熟练的工人真是幸运。

skim.en: After simmering the meat, skim the fat from the surface.
skim.zh: 把肉用文火炖过后再撇去表面的油脂。

skin.en: She had thick black hair and smooth dark skin.
skin.zh: 她一头浓密的黑发，皮肤黝黑光滑。

skin.en: The skin on his hands was dry and rough.
skin.zh: 他手上的皮肤干燥粗糙。

skinny.en: Some supermodels are far too skinny.
skinny.zh: 有些超级模特也太瘦骨嶙峋了。

skip.en: She skipped lunch in order to go shopping.
skip.zh: 为了去购物，她没有吃午饭。

skip.en: Williams skipped the game to be with his wife in the hospital.
skip.zh: 威廉斯为了在医院里陪他妻子而放弃了这场比赛。

skirmish.en: The young soldier was killed in a skirmish with government troops.
skirmish.zh: 这名年轻士兵在和政府军的一次小冲突中被打死了。

skirmish.en: Bates was sent off after a skirmish with the referee.
skirmish.zh: 贝茨和裁判发生冲突后被罚下场。

skirt.en: She wore a white blouse and a plain black skirt.
skirt.zh: 她穿着白衬衣和纯黑的裙子。

skirt.en: The old footpath skirts around the village.
skirt.zh: 古老的小径围绕着村庄。

skull.en: He can’t seem to get it into his skull that I’m just not interested in him.
skull.zh: 他这个笨蛋好像无法明白我根本对他不感兴趣。

sky.en: The sky grew dark, and a cold rain began to fall.
sky.zh: 天色转暗，开始下起冰冷的雨来。

sky.en: A shooting star sped across the night sky.

skyrocket.zh: 贸易逆差已经急剧增长。

slab.en: They used a slab of concrete as a lid.
slab.zh: 他们用一块水泥板当盖子。

slack.en: Keep the rope slack until I tell you to pull it.
slack.zh: 让绳子松着，直到我叫你拉紧。

slack.en: Business remained slack throughout the day.

slag.en: He’s always slagging her off behind her back.
slag.zh: 他老是在背后说她的坏话。

slam.en: We heard a car door slam.
slam.zh: 我们听到有车门砰的一声关上了。

slander.en: He is being sued for slander.
slander.zh: 他被控犯有口头诽谤罪。

slap.en: Sarah slapped Aaron across the face.
slap.zh: 萨拉在阿龙的脸上掴了一巴掌。

slap.en: Giles slapped his cards down on the table.
slap.zh: 贾尔斯把手里的牌啪的一声摔在桌上。

slate.en: There were several slates missing from the roof.
slate.zh: 房顶有几块石板瓦掉了。

slate.en: Doherty’s most recent novel has been slated by the critics.
slate.zh: 多尔蒂最新出版的小说受到了评论家的严厉批评。

slaughter.en: Hundreds of innocent civilians had been slaughtered by government troops.
slaughter.zh: 数百名无辜平民遭政府军屠杀。

slave.en: I’ve been slaving away at this report.
slave.zh: 我一直在拼命写这份报告。

slave.en: He’s been slaving over his history essay.
slave.zh: 他一直在拼命写历史课论文。

sleek.en: His hair was sleeked back with oil.
sleek.zh: 他的头发用发油向后梳理得平滑光亮。

sleep.en: I usually sleep on my back.

sleepy.en: The warmth from the fire made her feel sleepy.
sleepy.zh: 暖洋洋的炉火使她昏昏欲睡。

sleet.en: It was sleeting so hard we could barely see for 30 yards.
sleet.zh: 雨夹雪下得那么大，我们几乎看不到30

sleeve.en: Don’t worry. He still has a few tricks up his sleeve.
sleeve.zh: 别担心，他还有几个妙招没使出来呢。

slice.en: Everybody wants a slice of the profits.
slice.zh: 这利润每个人都想分一杯羹。

slick.zh: 这个展示会非常华而不实。

slick.en: He got round the defender using some slick footwork.
slick.zh: 他用灵巧的步法突破了后卫的防守。

slide.zh: 弗朗西丝卡从冰面上滑过。

slide.en: He opened the oven door and slid the pan of cookies in.
slide.zh: 他打开烤箱门，把甜饼烤盘滑了进去。

slight.en: I didn’t have the slightest idea who that man was.
slight.zh: 我根本不知道那人是谁。

slight.en: Derek felt slighted when no one phoned him back.
slight.zh: 没人给德里克回电话，他觉得自己受了冷落。

slightly.en: January’s sales were slightly better than average.
He was someone I already knew slightly.
slightly.zh: 他这个人我已略有所知。

slim.en: There’s only a slim chance that anyone survived the crash.
slim.zh: 这次失事有人生还的机会极为渺茫。

slim.en: The Republicans held a slim majority in the Senate.
slim.zh: 共和党在参议院中略占多数。

slip.en: Wright slipped but managed to keep hold of the ball.
slip.zh: 赖特滑了一下，但球还抓在手里。

slippery.en: In places, the path can be wet and slippery.
slippery.zh: 路上有些地方可能又湿又滑。

slippery.en: Harry’s palms were slippery with sweat.
slippery.zh: 哈里手心滑溜溜的都是汗。

slop.en: Coffee slopped over the rim of her cup.
slop.zh: 咖啡从她的杯口溢了出来。

slop.en: With each wave, more water slopped into the cabin.
slop.zh: 随着一个个浪头打来，更多的水漫进了船舱。

slope.en: She looked back up the grassy slope.
slope.zh: 她回头望了一眼那绿草如茵的坡地。

slope.en: We got to Tahoe on Friday, and hit the slopes (=skied on them) the next day.
slope.zh: 我们星期五到达塔霍，第二天就上坡滑雪了。

slot.en: Alan dropped another quarter into the slot on the pay phone.
slot.zh: 艾伦往付费电话的投币口里又塞了一枚 25

slot.en: A new comedy is scheduled for the 9 pm time slot.

slow.en: The car was travelling at a very slow speed.
slow.zh: 汽车正以非常慢的速度行驶。

slow.en: The economy faces a year of slower growth.
slow.zh: 经济将面临增长更缓慢的一年。

slowly.en: We are slowly but surely gaining the support of the public.
slowly.zh: 我们的确正逐渐赢得民众的支持。

sluggish.en: Alex woke late, feeling tired and sluggish.
sluggish.zh: 亚历克斯醒得很晚，感到很倦怠。

sluggish.en: Economic recovery has so far been sluggish.
sluggish.zh: 经济复苏的速度目前仍然缓慢。

sluice.en: He was sluicing down the table and the floor.
sluice.zh: 他正在冲洗桌子和地板。

slum.en: Jeremy doesn’t slum it when he goes away.
slum.zh: 杰里米出门在外是不会亏待自己的。

slumber.en: He passed into a deep slumber.

slump.zh: 她身子一歪倚在了墙上。

slump.en: Carol slumped back in her chair, defeated.
slump.zh: 卡萝尔颓然倒在椅子上。

slush.en: Children were sliding around in the snow and slush.
slush.zh: 孩子们在尚未化尽的雪地上到处滑行。

sly.en: He leaned forward with a sly smile.
sly.zh: 他俯身向前诡秘地一笑。

sly.en: They’d been seeing each other on the sly for months.
sly.zh: 他们已经偷偷约会了好几个月。

smack.en: He smacked the money down on the table and walked out.
smack.zh: 他啪的一声把钱扔在桌上就走了出去。

smack.en: He drained his glass and smacked his lips appreciatively.
smack.zh: 他一口气喝光了杯里的东西，满意地咂咂嘴。

small.en: The T-shirt was too small for him.
The sweater comes in three sizes – small, medium, and large.

smart.en: The smart kids get good grades and go off to college.
smart.zh: 聪明的孩子成绩好，可以去上大学。

smart.en: I was smart enough to wait for a week.
smart.zh: 我很明智，等了一个星期。

smash.en: Vandals had smashed all the windows.
smash.zh: 破坏分子打碎了所有的窗子。

smash.en: Firemen had to smash the lock to get in.
smash.zh: 消防员不得不砸锁而入。

smear.en: It left a black smear on his arm.
smear.zh: 这在他的左臂上留下了一点黑色的污迹。

smear.en: His face was smeared with mud.

smell.en: The air was filled with the smell of flowers.

smile.en: Susan smiled at him and waved.
She had to smile at his enthusiasm (=she was amused by it).

smoke.en: Smoke from burning fields drifted across nearby roads.
smoke.zh: 地里燃烧产生的烟雾飘到了附近的公路上。

smoke.en: He went outside for a quiet smoke.
smoke.zh: 他到外面去静静地吸一支烟。

smoker.en: My grandad was a heavy smoker (=someone who smokes a lot).
He had a smoker’s cough (=a cough caused by smoking cigarettes regularly).
smoker.zh: 他因为经常吸烟而得了咳嗽病。

smoking.en: I gave up smoking nearly ten years ago.
smoking.zh: 我差不多十年之前就戒烟了。

smooth.en: Her skin felt smooth and cool.
smooth.zh: 她的皮肤摸上去又滑又凉。

smooth.en: The stone steps had been worn smooth.
smooth.zh: 石阶被磨得光溜溜的了。

smoothly.en: It’ll take about three hours if everything goes smoothly.
smoothly.zh: 如果一切顺利的话，大约需要三小时。

smoothly.en: Donna keeps the office running smoothly.
smoothly.zh: 唐娜让办公室运转得很顺利。

smother.en: A teenage mother was accused of smothering her 3-month-old daughter.
smother.zh: 一个少女妈妈被指控闷死自己三个月大的女儿。

smother.en: The girls tried to smother their giggles.
smother.zh: 女孩们使劲忍住不笑出声来。

smuggle.en: The guns were smuggled across the border.
Illegal immigrants are smuggled into the country by boat.
smuggle.zh: 非法移民被小船偷运进这个国家。

smuggling.en: He was arrested in connection with drug smuggling.
smuggling.zh: 他因牵涉毒品走私被捕。

snack.en: Drinks and light snacks are served at the bar.
snack.zh: 酒吧里供应饮料和小吃。

snag.en: It’s an interesting job. The only snag is that it’s not very well paid.
snag.zh: 这是一份有趣的工作，唯一的缺憾是工资不高。

snag.en: The grand opening hit a snag when no one could find the key.
snag.zh: 盛大的开幕典礼上出了个小小的意外:

snail.en: Traffic was moving at a snail’s pace.
snail.zh: 车辆移动的速度慢得像蜗牛。

snake.en: A snake slithered across our path.
snake.zh: 一条蛇蜿蜒爬过我们的小路。

snake.en: The road snaked along the valley far below.
snake.zh: 公路在下面幽深的山谷里蜿蜒延伸。

snap.en: A twig snapped under my feet.
snap.zh: 一根细枝在我脚下嚓一声断开了。

snap.en: The wind snapped branches and power lines.
snap.zh: 大风刮断了树枝和输电线。

snatch.en: The thief snatched her purse and ran.
snatch.zh: 小偷抢了她的钱包就跑。

snatch.en: Keith snatches toys away from the other children.
snatch.zh: 基思把玩具从其他小孩那里抢走。

sneak.en: She snuck out of the house once her parents were asleep.
sneak.zh: 她父母刚一睡着她就溜出了家门。

sneer.en: She sneered at Tom’s musical tastes.
sneer.zh: 她嘲笑汤姆的音乐品位。

sneeze.en: The dust was making him sneeze.

sniff.zh: 玛格丽特可怜地抽泣着点了点头。

sniff.en: Stop sniffing and blow your nose.
sniff.zh: 别抽鼻子了，擤一擤鼻涕。

snipe.en: His former associates have been sniping at him in the press.
snipe.zh: 他从前的合伙人在报上诽谤他。

snob.en: I don’t want to sound like a snob, but I thought she was vulgar.
snob.zh: 我不想像个势利小人，但我觉得她就是庸俗。

snobbish.zh: 她家里人好像挺势利的。

snore.en: He could hear the old man snoring.
I heard a snore and knew he’d fallen asleep.
snore.zh: 我听见鼾声，就知道他已经睡着了。

snow.en: Snow was falling heavily as we entered the village.
snow.zh: 我们进村的时候雪下得正大。

snow.en: I could see footprints in the snow.

so.en: Why didn’t you call? We were so worried.
so.zh: 你为什么不打个电话？我们非常担心。

soak.en: Soak the clothes in cold water.
Let the pans soak; I’ll wash them later.
soak.zh: 把锅泡着吧，我过一会儿再洗。

soap.en: Wash thoroughly with soap and water.
soap.zh: 用肥皂和水彻底洗一洗。

soar.en: The price of petrol has soared in recent weeks.

他的表情立刻严肃起来。

so-called.zh: 那些所谓的专家说不出问题出在哪里。

society.zh: 英国现在是一个多种族社会。

sock.en: If they want promotion, United have got to pull their socks up.
sock.zh: 如果联队想要升级，那就得好好努力。

sock.zh: 拉里在他手臂上狠狠地打了一拳。

soft.zh: 我的双脚陷进了松软的地里。

soft.en: Cook the onions until they go soft.

soften.en: Use moisturizer to soften your skin.
soften.zh: 使用润肤霜让你的肌肤变柔滑。

soil.en: The soil here is very poor (=not good for growing crops).

soil.zh: 蔷薇适宜在黏质土中生长。

soldier.zh: 战斗中，有一名英国士兵受了伤。

soldier.zh: 没有他，我们还得坚持下去。

sole.zh: 格里菲思是此次撞车事故唯一的幸存者。

sole.en: The story was published with the sole purpose of selling newspapers.
sole.zh: 刊登这则报道的目的纯粹是为了推销报纸。

solely.en: Scholarships are given solely on the basis of financial need.
solely.zh: 奖学金完全是根据经济需要发放的。

solely.en: I shall hold you solely responsible for anything that goes wrong.
solely.zh: 出现任何差错的话，我唯你是问。

solemn.zh: 他们的脸突然变得严肃起来。

solemn.en: I’ll never be unfaithful again. I give you my solemn word.
solemn.zh: 我再也不会对你不忠了，我郑重向你保证。

solicit.zh: 摩根被指控非法征募竞选捐款。

solicitor.en: You need to see a solicitor.
A sign on the door read, ‘No Solicitors’.

solid.en: It was good to be back on solid ground again.
solid.zh: 又能踏上坚实的土地感觉真好。

solidarity.en: I come before you today to express my solidarity with the people of New York.
solidarity.zh: 今天我来到你们大家面前，是为了表示我对纽约人民的支持。

solidify.en: The volcanic lava solidifies as it cools.
solidify.zh: 火山熔岩冷却后变成固体。

solidify.en: The two countries signed a treaty to solidify their alliance.
solidify.zh: 两国签订了条约以巩固双方的联盟。

solitary.zh: 除了一个孤零零的身影，这些长凳上没有其他人了。
熊猫是喜欢独处的动物。

solitude.en: Carl spent the morning in solitude.
solitude.zh: 那天早上卡尔一个人很清静。

solo.zh: 里奇韦独自横渡大西洋的航行

solo.en: When did you first fly solo?
solo.zh: 你第一次单独飞行是什么时候？

solution.en: The best solution would be for them to separate.
solution.zh: 最好的解决方法是他们分开。

solution.en: There are no simple solutions to the problem of overpopulation.
solution.zh: 人口过多问题没有简单的解决方法。

solve.en: Charlie thinks money will solve all his problems.
solve.zh: 查理认为钱能解决他所有的问题。

solve.en: More than 70% of murder cases were solved last year.

solvent.en: I don’t know how we managed to remain solvent.
solvent.zh: 我不知道我们当时是怎么维持下来没有欠债的。

some.en: I need some apples for this recipe.
some.zh: 做这道菜我需要一些苹果。

some.en: My mother has inherited some land.
some.zh: 我母亲继承了一些土地。

somebody.zh: 不知谁的汽车警报器吵得我整晚都无法入睡。

someday.en: I’d like to visit Japan someday.
someday.zh: 我想将来有一天去日本。

someday.en: He hopes, someday, to have his own business.
someday.zh: 他希望有一天能够拥有自己的公司。

somehow.en: Don’t worry, we’ll get the money back somehow.
somehow.zh: 别担心，我们总会把那些钱拿回来的。

somehow.en: Somehow, I managed to lose my keys.
somehow.zh: 我不知怎的竟然把钥匙弄丢了。

someone.en: What would you do if someone tried to rob you in the street?
someone.zh: 要是有人在街上抢劫你，你会怎么办？

someone.en: Will someone please explain what’s going on?

something.en: Sarah said something about coming over later.
something.zh: 萨拉说她等一会儿过来什么的。

sometime.en: We’ll take a vacation sometime in September.
Our house was built sometime around 1900.

sometimes.en: I sometimes have to work late.
Sometimes, Grandma would tell us stories about her childhood in Italy.
sometimes.zh: 有时候，祖母会跟我们讲讲她儿时在意大利的经历。

somewhat.en: The price is somewhat higher than I expected.
somewhat.zh: 价格比我预料的高了一点。

somewhat.en: Things have changed somewhat since then.
somewhat.zh: 从那时候起，情况就有些不一样了。

somewhere.en: My wallet must be around here somewhere.
somewhere.zh: 我的钱包肯定是在这里的什么地方。

somewhere.en: There must be somewhere to eat cheaply in this town.
somewhere.zh: 镇上肯定有吃饭便宜的地方。

son.en: Her son Sean was born in 1983.
They have three sons and a daughter.
son.zh: 他们有三个儿子和一个女儿。

song.en: We used to listen to pop songs on the radio.
song.zh: 我们以前常常听收音机里播放的流行歌曲。

song.en: They sat round with guitars, singing songs.
song.zh: 他们弹着吉他围坐在一起唱民歌。

soon.en: David arrived sooner than I expected.
soon.zh: 戴维到得比我预料的快。

soothe.en: Lucy soothed the baby by rocking it in her arms.
soothe.zh: 露西把宝宝抱在怀里摇晃着，让他安静下来。

soothe.en: She made a cup of tea to soothe her nerves.
soothe.zh: 她泡了杯茶让自己平静下来。

sophisticated.en: Clarissa’s hair was swept up into a sophisticated style.
sophisticated.zh: 克拉丽莎的头发向后梳成一个很老成的式样。

sophisticated.en: British voters have become much more sophisticated.
sophisticated.zh: 英国的选民已经变得成熟多了。

sore.en: I had a sore throat and aching limbs.
My arms are sore from all the lifting.
sore.zh: 我搬东西搬到手臂酸痛。

sorrow.en: He expressed his sorrow at my father’s death.
sorrow.zh: 他对我父亲的去世表示悲痛。

sorrow.en: Claudia felt a deep pang of sorrow for the woman.
sorrow.zh: 克劳迪娅为这女人感到一阵深切的悲伤。

sorry.en: I’m really sorry. I didn’t mean to hurt your feelings.
sorry.zh: 非常抱歉，我不是有意要伤害你的感情。

sorry.en: I’m sorry, did I step on your foot?
sorry.zh: 对不起，我踩到你的脚了吗？

sort.en: What sort of shampoo do you use?
sort.zh: 你用的是哪一种洗发剂？

sort.en: I like all sorts of food – I’m not fussy.
sort.zh: 各种食物我都喜欢，我不挑剔。

soul.en: It was as if those grey eyes could see into the very depths of her soul.
soul.zh: 仿佛那双灰眼睛能看到她的灵魂深处。

soul.en: He is really quite a sensitive soul.

sound.en: There were strange sounds coming from the next room.
sound.zh: 隔壁房间传来奇怪的声音。

sound.en: She could hear the sound of voices.

soundly.en: The baby slept soundly all night.
soundly.zh: 宝宝整晚都睡得很香甜。

sour.en: Rachel sampled the wine. It was sour.
sour.zh: 雷切尔尝了尝葡萄酒，是酸的。

sour.zh: 伊丽莎又高又瘦，脸上阴沉沉的。

source.en: They get their money from various sources.
source.zh: 他们从各种途径弄到钱。

source.en: Beans are a very good source of protein.
source.zh: 豆类是很好的蛋白质来源。

south.en: By now, the army was approaching from the south.
south.zh: 那个时候军队正从南面逼近。

southwest.en: The plane flew southwest toward Egypt.
southwest.zh: 这架飞机朝西南方向飞往埃及。

souvenir.zh: 我买了一个埃菲尔铁塔模型作为去过巴黎的纪念品。

sovereignty.zh: 西班牙对这块领地的主权要求

sow.zh: 这些地里过去种的是燕麦。

space.en: There’s space for a table and two chairs.
space.zh: 能放得下一张桌子和两把椅子。

space.en: How much space is there on each disk?

spade.en: Beauty, intelligence, wealth – my mother had all of them in spades.

span.en: Over a span of ten years, the company has made great progress.
span.zh: 在十年时间里，这家公司取得了很大进展。

span.en: It’ll be difficult to hire that many new staff in such a short time span.
span.zh: 在这么短的时间里要想招聘到那么多新员工是很难的。

spar.zh: 他和维加一起练拳击时给打断了鼻梁骨。

spar.zh: 参议员们就医疗保健法案进行辩论。

spare.zh: 带一条毛巾和一些备用的衣服。

spark.en: The scrape of metal on metal sent up a shower of sparks.
spark.zh: 金属之间互相摩擦，迸出一串火星。

spark.zh: 蕾切尔看着她，感到了一线希望。

spatter.zh: 雨点开始噼里啪啦地打在石头上。

spawn.zh: 新技术创造了大量新的商机。

speak.zh: 上星期三我和她谈过了。

speak.zh: 我只是认得她，但没跟她说过话。

speaker.zh: 主要发言人是建筑师罗伯特·

speaker.zh: 一些英语单词对说其他语言的人来说是很难的。

spearhead.zh: 这个团体成了工会运动的

specially.zh: 这些船是专门为残疾人制造的。

specialty.zh: 约翰逊的专业是中世纪欧洲史。

species.zh: 已有七种猛禽被观察到。

specific.zh: 豪沃思先生给了我们很明确的指示。

specific.zh: 你能否更详细地说说你要找什么？

specifically.zh: 我明确地要求过你不要那样做！

specifically.zh: 具体来说，部门里希望以下问题得到解决。

specification.zh: 机场大楼是按联邦航空局的设计规格建造的。

specification.zh: 这些螺栓符合所有的工程设计规格。

specify.zh: 款项将在规定的几个月内支付。

specify.zh: 条例明确规定了维修人员的工作时长。

specimen.zh: 她的男朋友是体型很健美的那种人。

spectacle.zh: 审判变成了一场公开的闹剧。

spectacular.en: The news caused a spectacular fall in the stock market.
spectacular.zh: 这一消息引起了股市的暴跌。

spectrum.en: The bill drew support from across the political spectrum.
spectrum.zh: 这项议案得到了各个政治派别的支持。

spectrum.zh: 这里的两篇文章代表了两个极端的观点。

speculate.en: Jones refused to speculate about what might happen.
speculate.zh: 琼斯拒绝猜测可能会发生什么事情。

speculation.en: There is speculation that the president is ill.

speculation.zh: 这名证人的陈述纯粹是猜测。

speech.en: Each child had to give a short speech to the rest of the class.
speech.zh: 每个孩子都必须在全班同学面前作一个简短的演讲。

speech.zh: 他经常要发表席后演说。

speechless.zh: 他的那番话气得我说不出话来。

spell.en: Pupils should know how to spell commonly used words.
spell.zh: 小学生应该知道常用词的拼法。

spelling.zh: 她很快就正确地拼了出来。

spend.zh: 这星期我没有能力花更多的钱了。

spend.en: I only want to spend about $20.

spew.en: Factory chimneys spewed fumes out into the sky.
spew.zh: 工厂的烟囱向空中喷吐浓烟。

spew.en: Brown water spewed from the tap.
spew.zh: 褐色的水从龙头里喷了出来。

sphere.en: Women have often been excluded from positions of power in the public sphere.
sphere.zh: 女性常常被排除在公共领域的实权职位之外。

spice.en: Travel adds spice to your life.

spice.zh: 许许多多的人都买了这本书为他们的性生活增添乐趣。

spike.zh: 这橙汁里掺了杜松子酒。

spike.zh: 新装电话订单在过去两年里激增。

spill.zh: 凯蒂差点把牛奶洒出来。

spill.en: Oh no! I’ve spilt coffee all down my shirt!
spill.zh: 糟糕，我把咖啡洒得满衬衫都是！

spin.zh: 飞机的螺旋桨在快速旋转。

spin.en: She grabbed Norm’s arm and spun him around to face her.
spin.zh: 她抓住诺姆的胳膊将他转过来面对她。

spiral.en: Unemployment rose and the city went into a spiral of decline.
spiral.zh: 失业率上升，城市持续走下坡路。

spiral.en: The company is in a downward spiral.
spiral.zh: 这家公司越来越不景气。

spirit.en: I’m 85, but I still feel young in spirit.
She is a strong and independent spirit.
spirit.zh: 她是一个坚强独立的人。

spiritual.en: Painting helps fill a spiritual need for beauty.
spiritual.zh: 绘画可以满足对美的精神需求。

spiritual.en: Islam was inspired by the teachings of the spiritual leader Mohammed.
spiritual.zh: 伊斯兰教是受宗教领袖穆罕默德的教义影响产生的。

spit.en: Nick rolled down his window and spat.
spit.zh: 尼克摇下窗子，啐了口唾沫。

spit.en: A group of fans spat on the players as they left the field.
spit.zh: 一群球迷在球员离开球场时朝他们吐口水。

spite.en: We went out in spite of the rain.
spite.zh: 尽管下着雨，我们还是出去了。

spite.en: Kelly loved her husband in spite of the fact that he drank too much.
spite.zh: 虽然丈夫酗酒，凯莉仍然爱着他。

splash.en: The ocean splashed against the pier.
splash.zh: 海水哗啦哗啦地拍打着码头。

splash.en: He splashed cold water on his face.

splendid.en: The staff are doing a splendid job.
All the rooms have splendid views.
splendid.zh: 所有的房间都能看到漂亮的景致。

splendour.en: We marvelled at the splendour of the scenery.
splendour.zh: 我们对这壮丽的景色赞叹不已。

splendour.en: The palace has now been restored to its original splendour.
splendour.zh: 宫殿如今已恢复了它昔日的辉煌。

splinter.en: I’ve got a splinter in my finger.

splinter.zh: 这个曾经势力强大的党派现在已经四分

split.en: It was feared that the issue would split the church.
split.zh: 人们担心这一问题会导致教会分裂。

split.en: The party is split over the issue of immigration.
split.zh: 该党在移民问题上意见有分歧。

spoil.en: The whole park is spoiled by litter.
spoil.zh: 整个公园环境都给垃圾破坏了。

spoil.en: We didn’t let the incident spoil our day.
spoil.zh: 我们没有让这件事破坏我们一整天的气氛。

sponge.zh: 用湿布轻轻擦洗以清洁小地毯。

sponge.en: She stood on the bath mat and sponged herself down.
sponge.zh: 她站在浴室踏脚垫上，用海绵擦身子。

sponsor.zh: 伊士曼柯达公司是奥运会的主要赞助商。

sponsor.en: You cannot get a work visa without an American sponsor.
sponsor.zh: 如果没有美国担保人就拿不到工作签证。

sponsorship.en: The expedition is looking for sponsorship from one of the major banks.
sponsorship.zh: 探险队正在向一家大银行寻求赞助。

spontaneous.en: The crowd gave a spontaneous cheer.
My spontaneous reaction was to run away.
spontaneous.zh: 我的本能反应就是逃跑。

spoon.en: Spoon the mixture carefully into the bowls.
spoon.zh: 用匙小心地把混合料舀进碗里。

sporadic.en: There has been sporadic violence downtown.
sporadic.zh: 市中心时有暴力事件发生。

sporadic.en: The fighting continued sporadically for several days.
sporadic.zh: 战斗零零星星地持续了好几天。

sport.en: My favourite sports are tennis and swimming.
sport.zh: 我最喜欢的运动是网球和游泳。

sport.en: All students are encouraged to take part in a sport.
sport.zh: 鼓励所有的学生都要参加一项体育运动。

sportsman.zh: 他是个非常喜爱运动的人。

sportsmanship.en: His sportsmanship and style of play are refreshing.
sportsmanship.zh: 他的体育精神和比赛风格令人耳目一新。

sportsmanship.en: We try to teach the kids good sportsmanship.
sportsmanship.zh: 我们尽量教给孩子们良好的体育精神。

spot.en: I chose a spot well away from the road.
spot.zh: 我选了一个远离马路的地点。

spot.en: Why do they want to build a house on this particular spot?
spot.zh: 他们为什么要在这个地方建一栋房子？

spotlight.en: The yard was lit by three huge spotlights.
spotlight.zh: 院子里亮着三盏巨大的聚光灯。

spotlight.en: I was sweating under the spotlights.

spouse.en: Spouses were invited to the company picnic.
spouse.zh: 配偶受到邀请参加公司的野餐会。

spout.en: My plans for the weekend seem to have gone up the spout.
spout.zh: 我的周末计划看来已经泡汤了。

sprain.en: I fell down the steps and sprained my ankle.
sprain.zh: 我从台阶上摔下来，扭伤了脚踝。

sprain.en: I thought my wrist might be broken, but it was just a bad sprain.
sprain.zh: 我以为我的手腕可能摔断了，但只是严重扭伤。

sprawl.en: He sprawled out on the sofa.
sprawl.zh: 他摊开手脚躺在沙发上。

sprawl.en: I tripped on a stone and went sprawling on the pavement.
sprawl.zh: 我被一块石头绊了一下，四仰八叉地摔在人行道上。

spray.en: Someone had sprayed blue paint over his car.
spray.zh: 有人在他的汽车上喷了蓝色油漆。

spread.en: Fire quickly spread through the building.
He watched the dark stain spread over the gray carpet.
spread.zh: 他看着深色污渍在灰色地毯上漫开。

spring.en: It’s due to open in the spring.
It was a cold, sunny day in early spring.
spring.zh: 那是早春的一个晴朗的寒天。

springboard.en: The TV soap has been a springboard for a lot of careers.
springboard.zh: 电视肥皂剧是许多人事业的起点。

sprinkle.en: I sprinkled cocoa over my latte.
sprinkle.zh: 我在我的拿铁咖啡上撒了点可可粉。

sprint.en: He made a desperate sprint for the train.
sprint.zh: 他拼命地飞奔，追赶火车。

sprout.en: Move the pots outside when the seeds begin to sprout.
sprout.zh: 种子开始发芽时把盆搬到外面去。

sprout.en: Trees were starting to sprout new leaves.

spruce.en: Paul went upstairs to spruce up before dinner.
spruce.zh: 保罗在吃晚饭前上楼打扮了一下。

spruce.en: The cottage had been spruced up a bit since her last visit.
spruce.zh: 她上次来过以后，小屋收拾得整洁些了。

spur.en: We would often decide what to play on the spur of the moment.
spur.zh: 我们经常是凭兴致临时决定表演内容。

spur.en: It provided the spur to further research.
spur.zh: 这对进一步的研究起到了鼓舞作用。

spy.en: She worked as a spy for the American government.
spy.zh: 她为美国政府收集情报。

squander.en: The home team squandered a number of chances in the first half.
squander.zh: 主队在上半场浪费了几次机会。

squander.en: They squandered the profits on expensive cars.
squander.zh: 他们把利润挥霍在昂贵的汽车上。

square.en: The room is six metres square.
I don’t think the shelf is square with the floor.
square.zh: 我觉得这块搁板与地面不

squarely.en: He turned and faced her squarely.
squarely.zh: 他转过身来和她正面相对。

squarely.en: She hit him squarely on the nose.
squarely.zh: 她不偏不倚地打在他的鼻子上。

squash.en: The cake got a bit squashed on the way here.
squash.zh: 蛋糕在送来这里的路上有点压坏了。

squash.en: Her hair had been squashed down by her hat.
squash.zh: 她的头发被帽子压得平平的。

squat.en: He squatted down beside the little girl.
squat.zh: 他在小女孩身边蹲了下来。

squat.en: She lives in a squat in Camden.
squat.zh: 她在卡姆登私占了一间房子住着。

squeak.en: A rat squeaked and ran into the bushes.
squeak.zh: 一只老鼠吱吱叫着跑进了灌木丛。

squeal.zh: 孩子们高兴得尖叫起来。
他们开车走了，轮胎发出吱的一声。

squeeze.en: She smiled as he squeezed her hand.
squeeze.zh: 他捏了捏她的手，她笑了。

squeeze.en: He squeezed the trigger, but nothing happened.
squeeze.zh: 他扣动扳机，但没有反应。

squirrel.en: By December I had $300 squirreled away.
squirrel.zh: 到十二月份的时候，我已经存了 300

squirt.en: Water suddenly squirted out from a hole in the pipe.
squirt.zh: 突然有水从管子上的一个孔里喷射出来。

squirt.en: Squirt some oil in the lock.

stab.en: He was stabbed to death in a fight.
stab.zh: 他在一次打斗中被捅死了。

stab.en: She had been stabbed in the chest repeatedly.

stability.en: It could threaten the peace and stability of the region.
stability.zh: 这可能威胁到该地区的和平与稳定。

stabilize.en: The patient’s condition has now stabilized.
stabilize.zh: 病人的情况现已稳定下来了。

stable.en: A wide base will make the structure much more stable.
stable.zh: 宽大的底座会使结构牢固许多。

stable.en: He is said to be in a stable condition in hospital.
stable.zh: 据说他在医院里病情稳定。

stack.en: The assistants price the items and stack them on the shelves.
stack.zh: 售货员给商品标价，然后把它们叠放到货架上。

staff.en: Our department has a staff of seven.
The entire staff has done an outstanding job this year.
staff.zh: 今年全体员工工作都非常出色。

stage.en: It’s a good move at this stage in his career.
stage.zh: 在他事业的这个阶段，这是很好的一步。

stage.en: We’re getting to the stage where we hardly ever go out together.
stage.zh: 我们快要到几乎不一起外出的地步了。

stagger.zh: 他好不容易才蹒跚着走回家。

stagnate.en: Growth is expected to stagnate next year.

stain.en: Be careful you don’t stain the carpet.

stair.en: I left my briefcase at the top of the stairs.
stair.zh: 我把公文包遗忘在楼梯顶端了。

stake.en: They have to win the contract – thousands of jobs are at stake.
stake.zh: 他们必须拿下这份合同，这关系到数千个工作岗位。

stake.en: National pride is at stake in next week’s game against England.
stake.zh: 下星期对英格兰队的比赛关乎民族尊严。

stale.en: French bread goes stale (=becomes stale) very quickly.
Other marriages might go stale, but not theirs.
stale.zh: 别人的婚姻也许会变得平淡无味，但他们的婚姻不会。

stalk.en: We know the rapist stalks his victims at night.
stalk.zh: 我们知道那个强奸犯在夜间偷偷地跟踪受害人。

stalk.en: She was stalked by an obsessed fan.
stalk.zh: 她被一名痴迷的崇拜者跟踪。

stall.en: An inexperienced pilot may easily stall a plane.
stall.zh: 没有经验的飞行员会很容易使飞机失速下降。

stammer.en: Whenever he was angry, he would begin to stammer slightly.
stammer.zh: 他一生气说话就开始有点结巴。
本结结巴巴地道了个歉。

stamp.en: The speech bore (=had) the stamp of authority.
He’s clearly of a very different stamp.
stamp.zh: 他显然属于完全不同的一类人。

stance.en: What is your stance on environmental issues?
stance.zh: 你在环境问题上持什么立场？

stance.en: The president has adopted a tough stance on terrorism.
stance.zh: 总统对恐怖主义采取强硬的立场。

stand.en: It looks like we’ll have to stand – there are no seats left.

standard.en: Students have to reach a certain standard or they won’t pass.
standard.zh: 学生必须达到某一标准，否则无法通过。

standard.en: The airline has rigorous safety standards.
standard.zh: 这家航空公司有严格的安全标准。

standardize.en: Attempts to standardize English spelling have never been successful.
standardize.zh: 统一英语拼写的尝试从未成功过。

standing.en: You have to pay standing charges whether or not you use the service.
standing.zh: 无论是否使用这项服务，你都必须一直付费。

standing.en: A standing committee was established to coordinate the army and navy.
standing.zh: 成立了常务委员会以协调陆军和海军。

standpoint.en: Let’s look at the questions from an economic standpoint.
standpoint.zh: 让我们从经济的角度来看这些问题。

standstill.en: Strikers brought production to a standstill.
standstill.zh: 罢工者使生产陷于停顿。

staple.en: Bananas and sugar are the staples of Jamaica.
staple.zh: 香蕉和糖是牙买加的主要产品。

staple.en: The handouts are all stapled together.
staple.zh: 课堂讲义都是装订在一起的。

star.en: I lay on my back and looked up at the stars.
star.zh: 我仰卧着看天上的星星。

star.en: The sky was filled with stars.

starch.en: He eats a lot of starch.
starch.zh: 他吃大量含淀粉的食物。
避免食用高脂的和含淀粉的食物。

stare.en: She stared at me in disbelief.

stark.en: In the cold dawn light, the castle looked stark and forbidding.
stark.zh: 在寒冷的曙光中，城堡看上去了无生气，令人生畏。

stark.en: The movie shows the stark realities of life in the ghetto.
stark.zh: 这部影片展示了贫民区生活的严酷现实。

start.en: There’s so much to do I don’t know where to start.
start.zh: 有那么多的事情要做，我都不知道从哪里开始。
你开始做家庭作业了吗？

starter.en: We had soup as a starter, followed by steak.
starter.zh: 我们的第一道菜是汤，接下来是牛排。

starter.en: Of the seven starters, only three finished the race.
starter.zh: 参赛的七名选手中，只有三名跑完全程。

startle.en: Sorry, I didn’t mean to startle you.
startle.zh: 抱歉，我不是故意吓你一跳的。

startle.en: I was startled to see Amanda.
startle.zh: 看到阿曼达，我吃了一惊。

starve.en: Thousands of people will starve if food doesn’t reach the city.
starve.zh: 如果食品不能运到那座城市，成千上万的人就要饿死。

starve.en: They’ll either die from the cold or starve to death (=die from lack of food).
starve.zh: 他们要么会冻死，要么会饿死。

stash.en: He has money stashed away in the Bahamas.
You can stash your gear in here.
stash.zh: 你可以把你的装备存放在这里。

state.en: There are fears for the state of the country’s economy.
state.zh: 人们担心国家的经济状况。

state.en: When we bought the house, it was in a terrible state.
state.zh: 我们买下这栋房子时，它的状况很糟糕。

statement.en: In an official statement, she formally announced her resignation.
statement.zh: 在一份官方声明中，她正式宣布辞职。

statement.en: I haven’t received my bank statement for last month yet.
statement.zh: 我还没有收到上个月的银行结算单。

static.en: Economists predict that house prices will remain static for a long period.
static.zh: 经济学家预测，房价将长期保持稳定。

static.en: His promotion has caused a lot of static.
static.zh: 他的晋升引起很多人不满。

station.en: I want to get off at the next station.
Is there a waiting room in the station?

stationary.en: How did you manage to drive into a stationary vehicle?
stationary.zh: 你是怎么开车的，竟会撞上一辆停着的车子？

statistic.en: Statistics show that 50% of new businesses fail in their first year.
Statistics is a branch of mathematics.
statistic.zh: 统计学是数学的一个分支。

statue.en: Churchill’s statue stands outside the parliament building.
statue.zh: 丘吉尔的塑像矗立在议会大厦外。

statue.en: A bronze statue was erected in his honour.
statue.zh: 人们立了一座铜像纪念他。

stature.en: Armstrong was a musician of world stature.
stature.zh: 阿姆斯特朗是一位享誉全球的音乐家。

stature.en: He grew in stature (=became more admired or popular) during the campaign.
stature.zh: 在这场宣传活动中，他的声望提高了。

status.en: These documents have no legal status in Britain.
status.zh: 这些文件在英国并无法律效力。

status.en: What is your marital status (=are you married or not)?

statute.en: Protection for the consumer is laid down by statute (=established by law).
statute.zh: 保障消费者权益已有法律明文规定。

statute.en: College statutes forbid drinking on campus.
statute.zh: 大学校规禁止在校园内喝酒。

stave.en: The ship’s side was stove in when it went onto the rocks.
She brought some fruit on the journey to stave off hunger.
stave.zh: 她旅途上带了些水果充饥。

stay.zh: 他们待了整个下午聊天。

steadfast.en: Dr Faraday remained steadfast in his plea of innocence.
steadfast.zh: 法拉第医生坚持自己无罪的抗辩。

steal.en: Boys broke into a shop and stole £45 in cash.
steal.zh: 男孩们闯进一家商店，盗走了45

steal.en: He stole money from his parents.

steam.en: Steam rose from the hot tub.
steam.zh: 水蒸气从热腾腾的浴缸里升起。

steam.en: The engines are driven by steam.
steam.zh: 这些发动机是由蒸汽驱动的。

steel.en: Sheffield is a major steel town.
steel.zh: 谢菲尔德是主要的钢铁城市之一。

steel.en: He steeled himself not to look away.
steel.zh: 他硬下心不把目光移开。

steep.en: The road became rocky and steep.

steer.en: He was steering with only one hand.

stem.en: The measures are meant to stem the tide of illegal immigration.
stem.zh: 这些措施旨在遏制非法移民潮。

stem.en: A tight bandage should stem the bleeding.

step.en: He took one step and fell.
Tom took a step back and held the door open.
step.zh: 汤姆后退一步，把门撑开着。

stereo.en: He was listening to the Beatles on the car stereo.
stereo.zh: 他在听汽车立体声音响播放的披头士乐队的歌。

sterile.en: Radiotherapy has left her permanently sterile.
sterile.zh: 放射疗法造成她终身不育。

sterile.en: Rinse the eye with sterile water.
sterile.zh: 用消过毒的水冲洗眼睛。

sterilize.en: Sterilize the bottles with boiling water.
sterilize.zh: 用沸水把这些瓶子消毒。

sterling.en: Ella has done some sterling work.
sterling.zh: 埃拉做了一些出色的工作。

stern.en: His actions have earned him stern rebukes from human rights organizations.
stern.zh: 他的行为招致人权组织的严厉指责。

stern.en: Ann, made of sterner stuff than I, refused all offers of help.
stern.zh: 安比我性格坚强，她拒绝一切帮助。

stew.en: Let him stew – I'm not going to help him.

steward.en: Kissinger was now chief steward of US foreign policy.
steward.zh: 基辛格现在是美国外交政策的主要负责人了。

stewardship.en: Some critics have doubts about his stewardship of the nation.
stewardship.zh: 一些批评者对他管理国家的方式提出质疑。

stewardship.en: The farm was quite a different place under Mom’s stewardship.
stewardship.zh: 在妈妈的管理下，农场完全变了样。

stick.en: Someone had stuck posters all over the walls.
I could feel my shirt sticking to my back.
stick.zh: 我能感觉到衬衫贴在了背上。

sticky.en: There’s some sticky stuff in your hair.
sticky.zh: 你的头发上有什么黏糊糊的东西。

sticky.en: It was hot and sticky and there was nowhere to sit.
sticky.zh: 天气闷热潮湿，连个坐的地方都找不到。

stiff.en: Her legs were stiff from kneeling.
Her fingers were stiff with cold.

stiffen.en: He touched her, and she stiffened.
Their opposition only stiffened my resolve.
stiffen.zh: 他们的反对只是更加坚定了我的决心。

stifle.en: How can this party stifle debate on such a crucial issue?
stifle.zh: 该党怎么可以压制对这么一个重要问题的辩论？

stifle.en: He stifled an urge to hit her.
stifle.zh: 他强忍住冲动，没有打她。

stigma.en: The stigma of alcoholism makes it difficult to treat.
stigma.zh: 酗酒的恶名令其很难治愈。

stigma.en: There is a social stigma attached to single parenthood.
stigma.zh: 单身父母在社会上的名声不光彩。

still.en: Do you still have Julie’s phone number?
still.zh: 你还留着朱莉的电话号码吗？

still.en: I still haven’t finished painting the spare room.
still.zh: 我还没粉刷完那间空房间。

stimulant.en: Increases in new construction would be a stimulant to the economy.
stimulant.zh: 新建设项目的增加对经济可能是一种刺激。

stimulate.en: Her interest in art was stimulated by her father.
stimulate.zh: 她对艺术的兴趣是她父亲激发的。

stimulate.en: An inspiring teacher can stimulate students to succeed.
stimulate.zh: 一位具启发能力的教师能够激励学生取得成功。

stimulus.en: Tax cuts provided the stimulus which the slow economy needed.
stimulus.zh: 减税为不景气的经济带来了其所需的刺激。

stimulus.en: The discovery of oil acted as a stimulus to industrial development.
stimulus.zh: 石油的发现对工业发展是一个促进因素。

sting.en: He was stung by a bee.

stint.en: Mark did a two-year stint in the army.
They didn’t stint on food and drink at their wedding.
stint.zh: 他们在婚礼上毫不吝惜食物和饮料。

stipulate.en: Laws stipulate the maximum interest rate that banks can charge.
stipulate.zh: 法律对银行可以收取的最高利率作了规定。

stipulate.en: The regulations stipulate that everything has to comply to the relevant safety standards.
stipulate.zh: 条例规定凡事都要遵守相关的安全规范。

stipulation.en: The agreement included a stipulation that half of the money had to be spent on housing for lower-income families.
stipulation.zh: 协议中包含一项条款，规定这笔钱有一半必须用于低收入家庭的住房供给。

stir.en: Stir the paint to make sure it is smooth.
She stirred her coffee with a plastic spoon.
stir.zh: 她用塑料调羹搅拌咖啡。

stitch.en: He had to have ten stitches in his head.
stitch.zh: 他头上不得不缝了十针。

stitch.en: Purl and plain are the two main stitches in knitting.
stitch.zh: 反针和平针是编织中的两种主要织法。

stock.en: We have a huge stock of quality carpets on sale.
stock.zh: 我们备有大量优质地毯出售。

stomach.en: I was so hungry my stomach hurt.
His stomach was full of food.

stone.en: The floors are made of stone.
A handful of protesters began throwing stones at the police.
stone.zh: 有几个抗议者开始朝警察投掷石块。

stony.zh: 卡米拉冷冷地盯着前方。

stoop.en: We had to stoop to pass through the low entrance.
stoop.zh: 我们得弯腰通过那低矮的入口。

stoop.en: Dave stooped down to tie his shoes.

stop.en: By midday the rain had stopped.
This is where the path stops.

stoppage.en: We had five minutes of stoppage time (=extra time played in a sports match because of pauses) at the end of the first half.
stoppage.zh: 上半场结束前我们补时五分钟。

storage.en: They moved to a house with lots of storage space.
storage.zh: 他们搬到了一栋有很大贮存空间的房子里。

storage.en: I put some of my things in storage.
storage.zh: 我把我的一些东西存放起来。

store.en: At Christmas the stores stay open late.
store.zh: 在圣诞节期间，商店营业到很晚。

store.en: She worked in a grocery store before going to college.
store.zh: 她读大学前在一家杂货店打工。

storm.en: The weather forecast is for severe storms tonight.
storm.zh: 天气预报说今晚有强暴风雨。

storm.en: Twenty people were killed when the storm struck the Midwest.
storm.zh: 暴风雨袭击中西部，造成20

stormy.en: The sky was starting to look stormy.
stormy.zh: 开始变天了，看上去暴风雨将至。

story.en: Mommy, will you read me a story?
story.zh: 妈妈，给我读个故事好吗？

story.en: We cuddled together over a bedtime story.
story.zh: 我们依偎在一起看睡前故事。

stout.en: He put up a stout defence in court.
stout.zh: 他在法庭上进行了顽强的抗辩。

stow.en: I stowed my bag under the seat.
stow.zh: 我把包收好放到座位底下。

stow.en: A boy was caught trying to stow away on a plane.
stow.zh: 一个男孩试图逃票乘飞机被抓住。

straight.en: The book is on the table straight in front of you.
straight.zh: 那本书就在你面前的桌子上。

straight.en: She was looking straight at me.

straighten.en: Mum told me to straighten my room.
straighten.zh: 妈妈让我把自己的房间整理干净。

straightforward.en: Installing the program is relatively straightforward.
straightforward.zh: 安装这个程序相对来说比较简单。

straightforward.en: This area of law is far from straightforward (=complicated).
straightforward.zh: 法律的这个领域很复杂。

strain.en: I couldn’t look after him anymore; the strain was too much for me.
strain.zh: 我不能再照看他了，压力太大。

strain.en: Did you find the job a strain?
strain.zh: 你觉得这份工作紧张吗？

strait.en: After the war, the country’s economy was in dire straits.
strait.zh: 战后该国的经济陷入困境。

strait.en: The firm is now in dire financial straits.
strait.zh: 该公司目前财务状况极度困难。

strand.en: He reached out and brushed a strand of hair away from her face.
strand.zh: 他伸手拂去她脸上的一缕头发。

strand.en: Plato draws all the strands of the argument together.
strand.zh: 柏拉图把各个论点归结到一起。

strange.en: Does Geoff’s behaviour seem strange to you?
strange.zh: 你觉得杰夫的行为反常吗？

strange.en: She felt there was something strange about Dexter’s voice.
strange.zh: 她觉得德克斯特的声音有点奇怪。

stranger.en: Children must not talk to strangers.
stranger.zh: 小孩子千万不要同陌生人说话。

stranger.en: Julie finds it easy to speak to complete strangers.
stranger.zh: 朱莉觉得和素不相识的人讲话不是难事。

strap.en: The strap of my bag is broken.
He was only ten when he strapped on a guitar for the first time.
strap.zh: 他第一次背上吉他时才十岁。

strategic.en: UN forces made a strategic withdrawal.
strategic.zh: 联合国部队作了战略性撤退。

strategic.en: Marksmen were placed at strategic points along the president’s route.
strategic.zh: 在总统所经路线的要害地点上安排了神枪手。

strategy.en: It is the general’s role to develop overall strategy.
strategy.zh: 制定整体战略是将军的责任。

strategy.en: The company must first resolve questions of strategy.
strategy.zh: 公司首先必须解决规划问题。

stratification.en: The Indian caste system is an example of social stratification.
stratification.zh: 印度的种姓制度是社会阶层化的一个例子。

stratosphere.en: Oil prices soared into the stratosphere.
He’s now at the top of the political stratosphere.

straw.en: She sipped her lemonade through a straw.
Making me work late on Friday was the last straw.
straw.zh: 要我周五加班到很晚终于让我不堪忍受了。

stray.en: Three of the soldiers strayed into enemy territory.
stray.zh: 三名士兵误入敌军阵地。

stray.en: We’re straying into ethnic issues here.
stray.zh: 我们现在已偏离主题，讨论起种族问题了。

streak.en: Sue has blonde streaks in her hair.
streak.zh: 休的头发里夹杂着几缕金发。

streak.en: His serious nature was lightened by a streak of mischief.
streak.zh: 他严肃的个性中带着一丝顽皮。

stream.en: A steady stream of visitors came to the house.
stream.zh: 游客络绎不绝地来参观这所房子。

stream.en: A stream of cold air rushed through the open door.
stream.zh: 一股冷气穿过敞开的门直冲进来。

streamline.en: All these new cars have been streamlined.
streamline.zh: 所有这些新汽车都被设计成流线型。

street.en: We moved to Center Street when I was young.
street.zh: 在我小时候，我们搬到了中心大街。

street.en: She lives just a few streets away.
street.zh: 她的住处就在几条街外。

strength.en: She didn’t even have the strength to stand up.
strength.zh: 她甚至连站起来的力气都没有了。

strength.en: I’m trying to build up my strength.

strengthen.en: Our friendship has steadily strengthened over the years.
Steve’s opposition only strengthened her resolve to go ahead.
strengthen.zh: 史蒂夫的反对反而坚定了她继续下去的决心。

strenuous.en: The doctor advised Ken to avoid strenuous exercise.
strenuous.zh: 医生建议肯避免剧烈运动。

strenuous.en: Sherry’s been making a strenuous effort to lose weight.

stress.en: Your headaches are due to stress.
stress.zh: 你的头痛是压力造成的。

stress.en: Janet’s been under a lot of stress since her mother’s illness.
stress.zh: 珍妮特自从母亲生病以来承受了很大的压力。

stressful.en: Moving to a new house is a very stressful experience.
stressful.zh: 搬新家是件很劳心的事。

stretch.en: A spider’s web can stretch considerably without weakening.
stretch.zh: 蜘蛛网能拉得相当长而韧性不减。

stretch.en: Where can I buy those things that stretch your shoes?
stretch.zh: 在哪儿能买到把鞋撑大的东西？

stretcher.en: Ward was stretchered off early in the game.
stretcher.zh: 比赛开始不久，沃德就被人用担架抬下场。

strew.en: The street was strewn with broken glass.

strict.en: This company is very strict about punctuality.
strict.zh: 这家公司严格要求守时。

strict.en: The Stuarts are very strict with their children.
strict.zh: 斯图尔特夫妇待子女很严。

strictly.en: Alcohol is strictly forbidden on school premises.
The ban on hunting is not strictly enforced.
strictly.zh: 狩猎禁令并未严格执行。

stride.en: Paco reached the door in only three strides.
stride.zh: 帕科三大步就走到了门口。

stride.en: The government has made great strides in reducing poverty.
stride.zh: 政府在减少贫困方面已经取得巨大进展。

strike.en: She fell heavily, striking her head against the side of the boat.
strike.zh: 她重重地摔倒，头撞在船舷上。

strike.en: A snowball struck him on the back of the head.
strike.zh: 一个雪球打中了他的后脑勺。

strikingly.en: The two experiments produced strikingly different results.
strikingly.zh: 两个实验得出截然不同的结果。

string.en: Her key hung on a string around her neck.
string.zh: 她的钥匙穿了根绳子挂在脖子上。

string.en: I need a piece of string to tie this package.
string.zh: 我需要一根绳子来捆这个包裹。

strip.en: A strip of sand between the cliffs and the sea.
strip.zh: 悬崖和大海之间的一块狭长沙地
利物浦队著名的红色队服

stripe.en: Politicians of all stripes complained about the plan.
stripe.zh: 各个派别的政客都抱怨这项计划。

strive.en: I was still striving to be successful.
We must continue to strive for greater efficiency.
strive.zh: 我们必须继续为提高效率而努力。

stroke.en: She died following a massive stroke.
I looked after my father after he had a stroke.
stroke.zh: 我父亲中风后由我照看他。

stroll.en: We were strolling along, laughing and joking.
stroll.zh: 我们有说有笑，信步走着。

stroll.en: They went for a stroll in the park.

strong.en: He was a big strong man.

stronghold.en: The area is a Republican stronghold.
stronghold.zh: 这个地区是共和党的大本营。

stronghold.en: The fighters moved south to their mountain stronghold.
stronghold.zh: 战士们向南行进，到达他们在山上的据点。

strongly.en: I’m strongly opposed to capital punishment.
We strongly believe that she is innocent.

structural.en: The earthquake caused minor structural damage.
structural.zh: 这次地震造成了轻微的结构破坏。

structural.en: Is the building structurally sound (=in good condition)?
structural.zh: 这栋建筑物的结构状况还好吗？

structure.en: A new management structure has been introduced.
structure.zh: 已推行一种新的管理结构。

structure.en: These kids require a lot of structure and stability.
structure.zh: 这些孩子需要有序和稳定的生活。

struggle.en: She’s struggling to bring up a family alone.
struggle.zh: 她独自一人艰难地养活一家人。

struggle.en: The airline is struggling with high costs.
struggle.zh: 航空公司在努力应付高成本。

strut.en: I strutted around Chicago as if I were really somebody.
strut.zh: 我在芝加哥街头昂首阔步，好像自己真是个人物似的。

strut.en: The band strutted their stuff in a free concert.
strut.zh: 那支乐队在一场免费音乐会上一显身手。

stubborn.en: I’ve got a very stubborn streak (=a tendency to be stubborn).

student.en: There are plenty of job opportunities for engineering students.
student.zh: 学工程的学生有许多工作机会。

student.en: He’s obviously an excellent student of human nature.
student.zh: 显然他对人性的研究很深入。

studio.en: Depardieu is making a film with one of the big Hollywood studios.
studio.zh: 德帕迪约正在为好莱坞的一家大制片公司拍摄一部电影。

study.en: Recent studies show that women still get paid a lot less than men.
study.zh: 最近的调查表明，女性的薪水仍比男性的要低很多。

study.en: The study was carried out between January and May 2008.

stuff.en: I’ve got some sticky stuff on my shoe.
stuff.zh: 我鞋子上有什么黏糊糊的东西。

stuff.en: How do you think you’re going to fit all that stuff into the car?
stuff.zh: 你说这么多东西你怎么装进车里？

stuffy.en: It’s getting stuffy in here – do you mind if I open the window?
stuffy.zh: 这里越来越闷了，我开开窗行吗？

stuffy.en: Their wedding was stuffy and formal.
stuffy.zh: 他们的婚礼古板而正式。

stumble.en: In her hurry, she stumbled and spilled the milk all over the floor.
stumble.zh: 匆忙中她绊了一下，把牛奶洒得满地都是。

stumble.en: Vic stumbled over the step as he came in.
stumble.zh: 维克进来时在台阶上绊了一下。

stump.en: There was only a stump of the candle left.
The doctors were stumped and had to call in a specialist.
stump.zh: 医生们被难倒了，只好请来专家。

stun.en: Redfern stunned the crowd with a last-minute goal.
stun.zh: 雷德芬在最后一分钟进球，使观众很是震惊。

stun.en: The impact of the ball had stunned her.

stunt.en: Not many actors do their own stunts.
stunt.zh: 不是很多演员亲自表演特技动作。

stunt.en: Todd flew over the city in a hot-air balloon as a publicity stunt.
stunt.zh: 作为一种宣传噱头，托德乘坐热气球飞越城市上空。

stupid.en: That was a stupid thing to say.
I can’t believe Kate was stupid enough to get involved in this.
stupid.zh: 我简直不能相信凯特这么傻，会介入这件事情。

sturdy.en: That chair doesn’t look very sturdy.
sturdy.zh: 那把椅子看上去不太结实。

sturdy.en: They kept up a sturdy opposition to the plan.
sturdy.zh: 他们一直坚决反对那项计划。

style.zh: 古巴特色的黑豆和稻米

style.en: The dinner will be served buffet-style.

stylist.en: Renee was the top stylist at the salon.
stylist.zh: 勒妮是这家美发厅最好的发型师。

stylist.en: Billie Holiday, one of jazz’s most distinctive stylists

subdivide.en: Over time, developers subdivided the land.
subdivide.zh: 开发商们渐渐地把这块土地进行了再分割。

subdivide.en: The house was subdivided into apartments.
subdivide.zh: 房子又被分割成几个套间。

subdue.en: Police managed to subdue the angry crowd.
subdue.zh: 警察设法控制住了愤怒的人群。
拿破仑控制了大半个欧洲。

subject.en: Paul has strong opinions on most subjects.
subject.zh: 保罗在大多数问题上观点激烈。

subject.en: The subjects covered in this chapter are exercise and nutrition.
subject.zh: 本章涵盖的主题是运动和营养。

subjective.en: As a critic, he is far too subjective.
subjective.zh: 作为评论家，他过于主观。

subjective.en: The ratings were based on the subjective judgement of one person.
subjective.zh: 这些等级是基于个人的主观判断而定的。

subjugate.en: The native population was subjugated and exploited.
subjugate.zh: 土著人被征服，并遭受剥削。

subjugate.en: Her own needs had been subjugated to (=not considered as important as) the needs of her family.
subjugate.zh: 她自己的需要服从于她家庭的需要。

submerge.en: The tunnel entrance was submerged by rising sea water.
submerge.zh: 隧道入口被涨起的海水淹没。

submerge.en: Feelings she thought she’d submerged were surfacing again.
submerge.zh: 她以为已经抑制住的情感再一次涌上心头。

submission.en: Napoleon threatened to starve the country into submission.
submission.zh: 拿破仑扬言要让这个国家挨饿到屈服。

submission.en: His head was bowed in submission.

submissive.en: In those days, women were expected to be quiet and submissive.
submissive.zh: 那时的妇女都要寡言恭顺。

submit.en: All applications must be submitted by Monday.
submit.zh: 所有申请必须在星期一前递交。

submit.en: Derek has agreed to submit to questioning.

subordinate.zh: 女人以前是从属于男人的。

subordinate.en: These aims were subordinate to the main aims of the mission.
subordinate.zh: 和这次任务的主要目标相比，这些目标是次要的。

subscribe.en: You can subscribe to the magazine for as little as $32 a year.
She subscribes to an environmental action group.
subscribe.zh: 她定期捐款给一个环境行动组织。

subscription.en: Are you interested in taking out a subscription to ‘Newsweek’ (=arranging to buy it on a regular basis)?
subscription.zh: 你有兴趣订阅《新闻周刊》吗？

subscription.en: You may cancel your subscription at any time.

subsequent.en: These skills were passed on to subsequent generations.

subsequently.en: The book was subsequently translated into 15 languages.
Subsequently, the company filed for bankruptcy.
subsequently.zh: 随后，该公司申请了破产。

subside.en: Simon waited until the laughter subsided.
subside.zh: 西蒙一直等到笑声平息下来。

subside.en: The pains in his head had subsided, but he still felt dizzy and sick.
subside.zh: 他的头痛已经减轻，但仍感到眩晕和恶心。

subsidiary.en: All other issues are subsidiary to this one.
subsidiary.zh: 其他所有问题都是这个问题连带出来的。

subsidize.en: Farming is heavily subsidized (=subsidized a lot) by the government.
subsidize.zh: 农业得到政府的大量补贴。

subsist.en: We had to subsist on bread and water.
subsist.zh: 我们不得不靠面包和水维持生命。

subsist.en: Old people often have to subsist on very low incomes.
subsist.zh: 老人往往不得不依靠很低的收入来维持生计。

subsistence.en: Many of the families are forced to live at the subsistence level.
subsistence.zh: 很多家庭被迫生活在基本生活水准线上。

subsistence.en: The land provided subsistence and little more.
subsistence.zh: 这块土地只能提供人们的基本生活所需，别无富余。

substance.en: The leaves were covered with a strange sticky substance.
substance.zh: 树叶上覆着一层黏糊糊的怪东西。

substance.en: Plutonium 238 is one of the most toxic substances known to man.

substantial.en: We have the support of a substantial number of parents.
substantial.zh: 我们有相当多家长的支持。

substantially.en: The deer population has increased substantially in recent years.
substantially.zh: 近几年，鹿的数量大幅增长。

substantially.en: There are one or two minor differences, but they’re substantially the same text.
substantially.zh: 这些文本有一两处细微差异，但大体上是一样的。

substantiate.en: Katzen offered little evidence to substantiate his claims.
substantiate.zh: 卡曾拿不出什么证据来证明他的说法。

substantive.en: The State Department reported that substantive discussions had taken place with Beijing.
substantive.zh: 美国国务院称已经和北京方面进行了实质性的商谈。

substitute.en: Germany brought on a substitute at half time.
substitute.zh: 德国队在比赛半场时换上一名替补队员。

substitute.en: The coach has to find a substitute for Tim.

substitution.en: Coach Ross made two substitutions in the second half.
substitution.zh: 罗斯教练在下半场两次换人。

subtitle.en: The opera’s subtitle is ‘The School for Lovers’.
The book is subtitled ‘A Psychology of Masculinity’.

subtle.en: The pictures are similar, but there are subtle differences between them.
subtle.zh: 这些图片很相似，但它们之间有细微的差别。

subtle.en: The warning signs of the disease are so subtle that they are often ignored.
subtle.zh: 这种疾病的警示征兆不易察觉，因而往往被忽视。

subtlety.en: She argued her case with considerable subtlety.
subtlety.zh: 她非常巧妙地为自己的论点辩护。

subtract.en: If you subtract 30 from 45, you get 15.

suburb.en: Don’t you get bored living out here in the suburbs?
suburb.zh: 你住在这郊区难道不觉得无聊吗？

subway.en: Boston has the oldest subway system in the US.
subway.zh: 波士顿拥有美国最老的地铁运输系统。

succeed.en: She wanted to be the first woman to climb Mount Everest, and she almost succeeded.
succeed.zh: 她本想成为第一位登上珠穆朗玛峰的女性，而且差一点就成功了。

succeed.en: Scientists claim they have succeeded in finding a cure for cancer.
succeed.zh: 科学家声称他们发现了一种治疗癌症的方法。

success.en: The experiment was a big success.
I tried to contact him, but without success.
success.zh: 我试图联系他，但没有成功。

successful.en: Were you successful in persuading him to change his mind?
successful.zh: 你说服他改变主意了吗？

succession.en: She won the championship four times in succession.
He fired two shots in quick succession.

successive.en: The team has had five successive victories.
successive.zh: 这支球队已经连胜五场了。

successive.en: Successive governments have tried to deal with this issue.
successive.zh: 历届政府都试图解决这个问题。

successor.en: His successor died after only 15 months in office.
I’m sure she will be a worthy successor (=someone who is very good and deserves to be someone’s successor).
successor.zh: 我确信她会是个当之无愧的接班人。

succinct.en: Anderson put the same point more succinctly.
succinct.zh: 安德森把同样这一点解释得更加简明扼要。

succumb.en: Succumbing to pressure from the chemical industry, Governor Blakely amended the regulations.
succumb.zh: 屈服于化工行业的压力，布莱克利州长修改了条例。

succumb.en: Gina succumbed to temptation and had a second serving of cake.
succumb.zh: 吉娜抵挡不住诱惑，吃了第二份蛋糕。

such.en: Such behavior is just not acceptable in this school.
such.zh: 这类行为在本校绝不允许。

such.en: The rules make it quite clear what should be done in such a situation.
such.zh: 条例中明确规定了在这种情况下应当如何处理。

suck.en: Michael put the cigarette to his lips and sucked in the smoke.
suck.zh: 迈克尔把香烟放到唇边吸了一口。

suck.en: Jennie sucked up the last bit of milk shake with her straw.
suck.zh: 詹妮用吸管喝完最后一点奶昔。

sudden.en: Life is cruel, she thought, with a sudden rush of anger.
sudden.zh: 生活真残酷，她想，心头突然涌上一股怒气。

suddenly.en: I suddenly realized that there was someone following me.
suddenly.zh: 我突然意识到有人跟着我。

sue.en: If the builders don’t fulfil their side of the contract, we’ll sue.
sue.zh: 如果建筑商不履行合同，我们就要提出起诉。

sue.en: The company is suing a former employee.
sue.zh: 该公司正在起诉一名前雇员。

suffer.en: At least he died suddenly and didn’t suffer.
suffer.zh: 至少他死得突然，没有遭罪。

suffer.en: She’s suffering a lot of pain.

suffice.en: A few brief observations will suffice for present purposes.
suffice.zh: 简单的几回观察就足以满足现时的目的。

sufficiency.en: The war has affected the country’s economic sufficiency.
sufficiency.zh: 战争已经影响到了这个国家的经济富足。

sufficient.en: We can only prosecute if there is sufficient evidence.
sufficient.zh: 有了足够的证据，我们才能提出起诉。

sufficient.en: Unauthorized absence is sufficient reason for dismissal.
sufficient.zh: 旷工足以成为解雇的理由。

sugar.en: Do you take sugar in your coffee?
How many sugars do you want in your tea?
sugar.zh: 你的茶里要放几茶匙糖？

suggest.en: The zoo asked its visitors to suggest a name for the new baby panda.
suggest.zh: 动物园请游客提建议，给刚出生的大熊猫起一个名字。

suggest.en: Her mother suggested that she should go and see the doctor.
suggest.zh: 她妈妈建议她去看医生。

suggestion.en: The committee rejected the suggestion that houses should be built on this site.
suggestion.zh: 委员会否决了在这个位置建造房屋的提议。

suggestive.en: Her symptoms are suggestive of a panic disorder.
suggestive.zh: 她的症状类似于某种惊恐症。

suggestive.en: It was a huge sound, suggestive of whales calling each other.
suggestive.zh: 声音很大，就像是鲸鱼在互相召唤。

suicide.en: More people commit suicide at Christmas than at any other time.
suicide.zh: 圣诞节期间自杀的人比其他任何时候都多。

suicide.en: My mother attempted suicide on many occasions.

suit.en: She was wearing a black trouser suit.
Johnson has filed suit against her.
suit.zh: 约翰逊对她提起了诉讼。

suitable.en: We are hoping to find a suitable school.
suitable.zh: 我们希望能找到一所合适的学校。

suitable.en: The house is not really suitable for a large family.
suitable.zh: 这所房子并不适合大家庭居住。

suitably.en: We were relieved that Gordon had arrived at the wedding suitably dressed.
suitably.zh: 看到戈登穿着得体的衣服来参加婚礼，我们都松了一口气。

sullen.en: Bill sat in sullen silence and refused to eat his lunch.
sullen.zh: 比尔一声不响，闷闷不乐地坐着，不肯吃午饭。

sultry.en: Since the rain, the air had become heavy and still and sultry.
sultry.zh: 下雨后，空气变得凝重而闷热。

sultry.en: She threw Carlo a sultry glance.

sum.en: He owes me a large sum of money.
Bill wants to spend a large sum on modernizing the farm.
sum.zh: 比尔想花一大笔钱将农场现代化。

summarize.en: The authors summarize their views in the introduction.
summarize.zh: 作者在序言里概述了他们的观点。

summarize.en: To summarize, in most cases the schools were achieving the standards set.
summarize.zh: 总的说来，在大多数情况下这些学校都达到了所定的标准。

summary.en: A brief summary is given on a separate sheet.
The group produces a monthly summary of their research.
summary.zh: 该小组每个月出一份研究总结。

summer.en: The children play on the beach during the summer.
summer.zh: 夏天孩子们在海滩上玩耍。

summer.en: Miriam likes to relax in her garden in summer.
summer.zh: 夏天米丽娅姆喜欢在她的花园里休息。

summertime.en: It doesn’t rain much in the summertime.

summit.en: The two presidents agreed to hold a summit in the spring.
summit.zh: 两位总统商定在春天举行一次首脑会议。

summit.en: Many people have now reached the summit of Mount Everest.
summit.zh: 现在已有很多人成功登顶珠穆朗玛峰。

summon.en: Robert summoned the waiter for the bill.
summon.zh: 罗伯特召唤服务员结账。

summon.en: The president summoned Taylor to Washington.
summon.zh: 总统把泰勒召到华盛顿。

sunday.en: We’re going to a match on Sunday.
sunday.zh: 我们星期天要去看场比赛。

sunday.en: What are you doing Sunday? American English

sunlight.en: The water sparkled in the bright sunlight.
sunlight.zh: 水面在灿烂的阳光下闪闪发亮。

sunlight.en: The garden looked lovely in the evening sunlight.
sunlight.zh: 暮色下的花园显得十分秀丽。

sunny.en: Tuesday will be dry with sunny spells.

sunrise.en: A farmer’s day begins at sunrise.

sunset.en: We take the flag down at sunset.

sunshine.en: We had three days of spring sunshine.
sunshine.zh: 我们享受了三天的春日阳光。

sunshine.en: Couples strolled in the afternoon sunshine.
sunshine.zh: 一对对男女在午后的阳光下漫步。

super.en: Sorry, I’m super tired, I have to turn in.
super.zh: 对不起，我累得很，得上床睡觉了。

superficial.en: Even a superficial inspection revealed serious flaws.
superficial.zh: 即使是粗略的检查都发现了严重的缺陷。

superficial.en: Despite their superficial similarities, the two novels are, in fact, very different.
superficial.zh: 这两本小说尽管表面上有相似之处，但实际上大不一样。

superior.en: Fletcher’s superior technique brought him victory.
superior.zh: 弗莱彻更胜一筹的技术使他取得了胜利。

superior.en: Your computer is far superior to mine.
superior.zh: 你的电脑比我的强多了。

superiority.zh: 美国在空中力量上的优势

superiority.en: Janet always spoke with an air of superiority.
superiority.zh: 珍妮特说话时总显得盛气凌人。

supersede.en: Their map has since been superseded by photographic atlases.
supersede.zh: 他们的地图从此被摄影地图册取代。

supervise.zh: 格里菲思密切指导该项研究。

supervision.zh: 宝宝时刻都要有人照看。

supervision.en: Costumes and sets were also made under his supervision.
supervision.zh: 服装和布景也由他负责。

supper.en: Why don’t you come over for supper on Friday?
supper.zh: 周五为什么不过来吃晚饭呢？

supper.en: We had supper in a small Italian place.
supper.zh: 我们在一家意大利小餐馆吃了晚饭。

supplant.en: Barker was soon supplanted as party leader.
supplant.zh: 巴克在党内的领导地位很快就被人取代了。

supplement.en: The payments are a supplement to his usual salary.
supplement.zh: 这些钱是他平常工资之外的补充。

supplement.en: Single rooms are available at a supplement.

supply.en: I’ve only got a week’s supply of tablets left.
supply.zh: 剩下的药片只够我一周的量了。

supply.en: There was a plentiful supply of cheap labour.

support.en: The bill was supported by a large majority in the Senate.
support.zh: 这项法案得到参议院绝大多数人的支持。

support.en: We need to support our teachers in their efforts to raise standards.
support.zh: 我们必须支持我们的教师为提高教学水准所作的努力。

supportive.en: My family were very supportive throughout the divorce.
supportive.zh: 离婚过程中我的家人自始至终都很支持我。

suppose.en: So things worked out for the best, I suppose.

supposedly.en: How could a supposedly intelligent person be so stupid?
supposedly.zh: 一个所谓的聪明人怎么会这么愚蠢？

supposedly.en: Anne is coming for a visit in March, supposedly.

supposition.en: His version of events is pure supposition.
supposition.zh: 他对事情的说法纯属推测。

supposition.en: The police are acting on the supposition that she took the money.
supposition.zh: 警方的做法是假定她拿了钱。

suppress.zh: 起义受到了残酷的镇压。

suppress.en: The police were accused of suppressing evidence.

supremacy.en: Japan’s unchallenged supremacy in the field of electronics
supremacy.zh: 日本在电子领域无人挑战的领先地位

supreme.en: It required a supreme effort to stay awake.
supreme.zh: 要保持清醒需要极大的努力。

sure.en: I’m sure there’s a logical explanation for all this.
sure.zh: 我确信这一切都是有合理解释的。

sure.en: Are you sure that you know how to get there?
sure.zh: 你肯定知道怎样到那里去吗？

surely.en: You must have heard about the riots, surely?
surely.zh: 想必你已经听说骚乱的事了吧？

surely.en: There must surely be some explanation.

surface.en: Dead leaves floated on the surface of the water.
surface.zh: 凋落的树叶漂浮在水面。

surface.en: Nearly 10% of the Earth’s surface is covered by ice.

surfing.en: When we were in Hawaii, we went surfing every day.
surfing.zh: 我们在夏威夷时每天都去冲浪。

surge.en: The crowd surged through the gates.

surgery.en: She required surgery on her right knee.
He underwent surgery for lung cancer.

surgical.en: With surgical precision he cut four inches off the legs of the jeans.
surgical.zh: 他以外科手术般的精准从牛仔裤上剪下四英寸长的裤管。
这个肿块通过手术切除了。

surmise.en: When she came in, he didn’t look up, so she surmised that he was in a bad mood.
surmise.zh: 他进来时低着头，因此她猜想他心情不好。

surmise.en: Charles was glad to have his surmise confirmed.
surmise.zh: 查尔斯很高兴他的推测得到了证实。

surmount.en: He has had to surmount immense physical disabilities.
surmount.zh: 他不得不克服严重的身体残疾。

surpass.en: He had surpassed all our expectations.
surpass.zh: 他超越了我们所有的预期。

surpass.en: The number of multiple births has surpassed 100,000 for the first time.

surplus.en: Any surplus can be trimmed away.
surplus.zh: 多出来的部分可以修剪掉。
埃塞俄比亚没有多余的食物。

surprise.en: What a surprise to find you here!
surprise.zh: 真想不到啊，在这儿碰到你！

surprise.en: We had a big surprise when we found out the truth.
surprise.zh: 我们知道真相后大吃一惊。

surprising.en: She told me a surprising thing.
surprising.zh: 她告诉我一件令人吃惊的事。

surprising.en: A surprising number of his paintings have survived.
surprising.zh: 他的存世画作多得出奇。

surprisingly.en: Not surprisingly, with youth unemployment so high, some school-leavers with qualifications fail to find jobs.
surprisingly.zh: 年轻人失业率如此之高，难怪一些具备专业资格的中学毕业生会找不到工作。

surrender.en: The terrorists were given ten minutes to surrender.
surrender.zh: 恐怖分子被限定在十分钟之内投降。

surround.en: The field was surrounded by trees.
He glared at the people who surrounded the tent.
surround.zh: 他怒视着围住帐篷的那些人。

surrounding.en: Troops sealed off the surrounding area.
We decided to explore the surrounding countryside.
surrounding.zh: 我们决定去附近的乡间走走看看。

surroundings.en: He switched on the light and examined his surroundings.
surroundings.zh: 他打开灯，查看了周围的情况。

surroundings.en: I need to work in pleasant surroundings.
surroundings.zh: 我需要在舒适的环境下工作。

survey.en: We conducted a survey of parents in the village.
survey.zh: 我们对这个村子的孩子父母作了一次调查。

survey.en: The survey showed that Britain’s trees are in good health.
survey.zh: 调查显示英国的树木状况良好。

survival.en: Illegal hunting is threatening the survival of the species.
survival.zh: 非法狩猎正威胁着物种的生存。

survival.en: The doctors gave him a one in ten chance of survival.
survival.zh: 医生说他有十分之一的生存希望。

survivor.en: Emergency help is needed for survivors of the earthquake.
survivor.zh: 地震的幸存者需要紧急援助。

survivor.en: She was the sole survivor (=only survivor) of the massacre.
survivor.zh: 她是大屠杀唯一的幸存者。

susceptible.en: Older people are more susceptible to infections.
Soil on the mountain slopes is very susceptible to erosion.
susceptible.zh: 山坡上的土壤很容易受到侵蚀。

suspect.en: I suspected that there was something wrong with the engine.
suspect.zh: 我怀疑发动机出了什么故障。

suspect.en: She strongly suspected he was lying to her.
suspect.zh: 她非常怀疑他在对她撒谎。

suspend.en: Sales of the drug will be suspended until more tests are completed.
suspend.zh: 这种药品在完成进一步检验之前将暂停销售。

suspend.en: Talks between the two countries have now been suspended.
suspend.zh: 两国间的对话现已中止。

suspense.en: They kept us in suspense for over two hours.
suspense.zh: 他们让我们提心吊胆了两个多小时。

suspense.en: Come on then, tell me what happened; the suspense is killing me (=I feel very excited or anxious because I do not know what will happen next).
suspense.zh: 快来，告诉我发生了什么事。急死我了。

suspension.en: Both sides are now working towards a suspension of hostilities.
suspension.zh: 现在双方都在朝着消除敌意的方向努力。

suspension.en: He received a six-month suspension for unprofessional behaviour.
suspension.zh: 他因有违职业道德的行为被停职六个月。

suspicion.en: I can’t say for definite who did it, but I certainly have my suspicions.
suspicion.zh: 我不能确切说是谁干的，但我肯定有怀疑的对象。

suspicion.en: Police suspicions were confirmed when the stolen property was found in his flat.
suspicion.zh: 失窃物品在他公寓里找到，警方的怀疑得到了证实。

suspicious.en: Some of his colleagues at work became suspicious of his behaviour.
suspicious.zh: 他的一些同事开始怀疑他的行为。

suspicious.en: They were suspicious about my past.

sustain.en: She found it difficult to sustain the children’s interest.
sustain.zh: 她发现很难保持孩子们的兴趣。

sustain.en: He was incapable of sustaining close relationships with women.
sustain.zh: 他无法和女人维持亲密关系。

sustainable.en: The government should do more to promote sustainable agriculture.
sustainable.zh: 政府应该做更多工作来推动可持续农业的发展。

sustainable.en: Cycling is a totally sustainable form of transport.
sustainable.zh: 骑自行车是一种绝对环保的交通方式。

sustenance.en: Without sustenance, the animals will soon die.
sustenance.zh: 没有食物，动物很快就会死亡。

sustenance.en: Potatoes were their only means of sustenance.
sustenance.zh: 马铃薯是他们唯一的食物。

swallow.en: He swallowed the last of his coffee and asked for the bill.
swallow.zh: 他喝完最后一口咖啡，要求结账。

swallow.en: Most snakes swallow their prey whole.
swallow.zh: 大多数蛇都是把猎物囫囵吞下。

swamp.en: We’ve been swamped with phone calls since the advert appeared.
swamp.zh: 自从广告出来后，电话多得使我们应接不暇。

swamp.en: In the summer the village is swamped by visitors.

swan.en: He’s gone swanning off to Rome for the weekend!
swan.zh: 他到罗马潇洒度周末去了！

swarm.en: Swarms of tourists jostled through the square.
swarm.zh: 一群群游客推推搡搡地穿过广场。

swarm.en: Photographers were swarming around the princess.
swarm.zh: 摄影师们一窝蜂地围在公主身边。

sway.en: The trees swayed gently in the breeze.
sway.zh: 树木在和风中轻轻摇曳。

sway.en: Don’t allow yourself to be swayed by his promises.
sway.zh: 你可不要听了他的许诺就改变主意呀。

swear.en: Don’t swear in front of the children.
swear.zh: 不要在孩子们面前说粗话。

swear.en: He turned round and swore at me.

sweat.en: I was sweating a lot despite the air conditioning.
sweat.zh: 尽管开着空调，我仍是满头大汗。

sweat.en: Within minutes she was sweating profusely.
sweat.zh: 不一会儿她就大汗淋漓了。

sweaty.en: We came home hot and sweaty after the day’s work.
sweaty.zh: 一天工作之后，我们回到家时热得满身是汗。

sweep.en: Bert swept the path in front of the house.
sweep.zh: 伯特清扫了屋前的小路。

sweep.en: Will you sweep the leaves off the patio?
sweep.zh: 你把露台上的落叶扫掉好吗？

sweet.en: How sweet of you to remember my birthday!
sweet.zh: 你真好，还记得我的生日！

sweeten.en: Sweeten the mixture with a little honey.
Old age had not sweetened her.
sweeten.zh: 上了年纪并没让她变得平和。

sweetheart.en: Members of the council had arranged a sweetheart deal with CTS.

sweetness.en: She’s all sweetness and light when Paul’s around.
sweetness.zh: 有保罗在，她就表现得特别甜美可爱。

sweetness.en: Life is not all sweetness and light.
sweetness.zh: 生活并不总是一帆风顺的。

swell.en: Her ankle was already starting to swell.
swell.zh: 她的脚踝已经开始肿起来了。

swell.en: The window frame had swollen shut.
swell.zh: 窗框膨胀变形，关得死死的。

swerve.en: The car swerved sharply to avoid the dog.
swerve.zh: 车子猛地急转，以避开那条狗。

swerve.en: The bus swerved off the road.
swerve.zh: 公共汽车突然转向驶离了马路。

swift.en: My letter received a swift reply.
swift.zh: 我的信很快就得到了回复。

swift.en: She shot a swift glance at Paul.

swim.en: We swam in the chilly water.
swim.zh: 我们在冰冷的水里游泳。

swim.en: She could swim across the lake.

swimmer.en: We watched the swimmers heading out across the lake.
swimmer.zh: 我们看着游泳的人向湖对岸游去。

swing.en: Let your arms swing as you walk.
He was swinging his bag back and forth.

swipe.en: She swiped me across the face.
swipe.zh: 她扬起手打了我一个耳光。

swipe.en: He jumped forward, intending to swipe at her.

swirl.en: He swirled the brandy around in his glass.
swirl.zh: 他旋动杯中的白兰地酒。

switch.en: She worked as a librarian before switching to journalism.
switch.zh: 她在转行从事新闻工作前是图书馆管理员。

switch.en: Duval could switch easily from French to English.
switch.zh: 杜瓦尔可以在法语和英语之间自如切换。

sword.en: The treaty hung like a sword of Damocles over French politics.
sword.zh: 这个条约好像一把达摩克利斯之剑悬在法国政坛之上。

syllabus.en: Two Shakespeare plays are on this year’s English syllabus.
syllabus.zh: 今年的英语课程大纲上有两部莎士比亚剧作。

symbol.en: The symbol on the packet is a guarantee that the food has been produced organically.
symbol.zh: 包装盒上的这个标识保证这种食物是有机生产的。

symbol.en: The dove is a symbol of peace.

symbolic.en: The protest was a symbolic gesture of anger at official policy.
symbolic.zh: 这次抗议是对官方政策极度不满的一种表示。

symbolic.en: It was a largely symbolic gesture from a government trying to win support.
symbolic.zh: 这在很大程度上是政府希望赢得支持所作出的象征性姿态。

symbolize.en: Crime often symbolizes a wider social problem.
symbolize.zh: 犯罪问题往往反映出更广泛的社会问题。

symbolize.en: Growing discontent has been symbolized by the protests.
symbolize.zh: 与日俱增的不满通过一次又一次的抗议表现出来。

symmetry.en: There was a certain symmetry to coming back to New York, where I started my artistic life all those years ago.
symmetry.zh: 人生的经历似乎是对称的，我又回到了纽约，那里是我早年开始艺术生涯的地方。

sympathetic.en: I’m sympathetic to parents who are worried about what their children see on television.
sympathetic.zh: 我很同情那些担心孩子所看电视内容的家长。

sympathetic.en: We hope always to provide a friendly sympathetic ear (=someone willing to listen to someone else’s problems).
sympathetic.zh: 我们希望总能做到友善地倾听。

sympathize.en: I sympathize, but I don’t know how to help.
sympathize.zh: 我很同情，但不知道如何帮忙。

sympathize.en: I can sympathize with those who have lost loved ones.
sympathize.zh: 我同情那些失去至爱的人。

sympathy.en: I have a lot of sympathy for her; she had to bring up the children on her own.
I have absolutely no sympathy for students who get caught cheating in exams.
sympathy.zh: 我对考试作弊被抓到的学生绝不同情。

symptom.en: Common symptoms of diabetes are weight loss and fatigue.
symptom.zh: 糖尿病的常见症状是消瘦和疲劳。

symptom.en: The disappearance of jobs is a symptom of a deeper socioeconomic change.
symptom.zh: 工作岗位减少是社会经济发生进一步变化的一个征兆。

synchronize.en: Businesses must synchronize their production choices with consumer choices.
synchronize.zh: 企业的产品品类必须与消费者的选择保持一致。

synonymous.en: Nixon’s name has become synonymous with political scandal.
synonymous.zh: 尼克松的名字成了政治丑闻的代名词。

synthesize.en: DDT is a pesticide that was first synthesized in 1874.

system.en: We’ve got a good system for dealing with complaints from customers.
system.zh: 我们有一套处理顾客投诉的良好制度。

system.en: I don’t understand your filing system.
system.zh: 我不明白你们的归档方法。

table.en: The food was served on long tables.
table.zh: 食物放在长餐桌上供应。

table.en: I've booked a table for two.

tablet.en: She took a couple of headache tablets.
The programme should not be set in tablets of stone, but improved continuously.
tablet.zh: 此方案不应固定不变，而应不断改进。

taboo.en: It’s taboo to date a man a lot younger than you.
taboo.zh: 和一个比自己年轻许多的男人约会是社会禁忌。

tack.en: If that doesn’t work, we’ll try a different tack.
tack.zh: 如果那样不行，我们将试试别的方法。

tack.en: Rudy changed tack, his tone suddenly becoming friendly.
tack.zh: 鲁迪改变策略，语气突然变得友好起来。

tackle.en: There is more than one way to tackle the problem.
tackle.zh: 解决这个问题不止一个办法。

tackle.en: It took twelve fire engines to tackle the blaze.

tact.en: With great tact, Clive persuaded her to apologize.
tact.zh: 克莱夫十分巧妙地说服了她去道歉。

tactful.en: There was no tactful way of phrasing what he wanted to say.
tactful.zh: 没有办法婉转地表达他想说的话。

tactic.en: Republicans accuse Democrats of using delaying tactics (=something you do in order to give yourself more time) to prevent a final vote on the bill.
tactic.zh: 共和党指责民主党采取拖延战术来阻止议案的最终票决。

tactic.en: Shock tactics are being used in an attempt to stop drink drivers.

tag.en: All the staff wore name tags.
tag.zh: 所有员工都佩戴姓名牌。

tag.en: His speed earned him the tag of ‘the runner’.

tail.en: We saw the tail of the procession disappearing round the corner.
tail.zh: 我们看到队伍的尾巴绕过拐角渐渐消失。

tailor.en: Treatment is tailored to the needs of each patient.
tailor.zh: 治疗方案是针对各个病人的需要而制订的。

tailor.en: The classes are tailored to suit learners’ needs.
tailor.zh: 课程根据学习者的需要而设计。

taint.en: Baker argues that his trial was tainted by negative publicity.
taint.zh: 贝克抗辩说他的审判受到了负面宣传的影响。

taint.en: The water had been tainted with a deadly toxin.

take.en: Barney took us to the airport.
Would you mind taking Susie home?

tale.en: He was in the middle of telling me a long tale about how he once met Bob Dylan.
tale.zh: 他正在和我絮絮叨叨地讲他有一次遇见红人队主教练的事。

tale.en: Don’t go telling tales to the teacher!

talent.en: He has a lot of talent, and his work is fresh and interesting.
talent.zh: 他很有天赋，作品新颖有趣。

talent.en: She showed a talent for acting at an early age.
talent.zh: 她在很小的时候就显示出了表演天赋。

talk.en: I could hear Sarah and Andy talking in the next room.
talk.zh: 我听到萨拉和安迪在隔壁讲话。

talk.en: English people love to talk about the weather.
talk.zh: 英格兰人喜欢谈论天气。

tall.en: This bush grows tall very quickly.
tall.zh: 这种灌木很快就能长高。

tally.en: Keep a tally of (=write down) the number of cars that pass.

tame.en: Most of the criticism has been pretty tame.
tame.zh: 评论的大部分内容很乏味。

tame.en: I decided that teaching was too tame for me.
tame.zh: 我最终认为教书对我来说太枯燥。

tamper.en: He noticed that the instruments had been tampered with.
tamper.zh: 他注意到仪器被人动过了。

tamper.en: I don’t see the point in tampering with a system that’s worked fine so far.
tamper.zh: 我不明白一个系统运行得好好的，改它干吗。

tan.en: She has a pale skin which doesn’t tan easily.
tan.zh: 她的肤色很白，不容易被晒黑。

tan.en: I wish I could get a tan like that.
tan.zh: 但愿我也能晒成那样的棕褐色肤色。

tang.en: The beer had a sharp, bitter tang.
tang.zh: 这种啤酒有一股强烈的苦味。

tangible.en: The scheme must have tangible benefits for the unemployed.
tangible.zh: 这个计划一定要对失业者有实实在在的好处。

tangible.en: He has no tangible evidence of John’s guilt.
tangible.zh: 他没有确凿的证据证明约翰有罪。

tangle.en: His parachute became tangled in the wheels of the plane.
tangle.zh: 他的降落伞缠在了飞机的轮子上。

tank.en: Somehow the chemical got from a storage tank into water supplies.
tank.zh: 不知怎么的，这种化学物从储存箱进入了供水系统。

tantamount.en: To leave a dog home alone is tantamount to cruelty.
tantamount.zh: 把狗独自留在家里等于虐待。

tap.en: Tap water (=water that comes out of a tap) is usually heavily treated with chemicals.
tap.zh: 自来水一般都用化学品严格处理过。

tap.en: She went into the bathroom and turned on the taps.
tap.zh: 她走进浴室，打开水龙头。

tape.en: We’ve got the film on tape.
I hate hearing my voice on tape.
tape.zh: 我不喜欢听我录在磁带上的声音。

tapestry.en: This was all new to her – part of life’s rich tapestry.
tapestry.zh: 这是七彩生活的一部分——

tar.en: You’ve made it very clear that you think I’m tarred with the same brush as William.
tar.zh: 你已经十分明确地表示，你认为我和威廉是一丘之貉。

target.en: Higher degrees in English are a target for foreign students.
target.zh: 获得英语高等学位是外国学生的目标。

target.en: There is no target date for completion of the new project.
target.zh: 这个新的项目何时完工没有预定日期。

tariff.en: The government may impose tariffs on imports.
tariff.zh: 政府可能要对进口货物征收关税。

tarnish.en: His regime was tarnished by human rights abuses.
tarnish.zh: 他的政权因践踏人权而形象受损。

task.en: The task of the union representative is to fight on behalf of the members.
task.zh: 工会代表的任务就是为工会成员争取利益。

task.en: Sara had the task of preparing the agenda for meetings.
task.zh: 萨拉的任务是准备会议议程。

taste.en: The medicine had a slightly bitter taste.
I don’t really like the taste of meat anymore.
taste.zh: 我已经不太喜欢肉的味道了。

taut.en: Catherine looked upset, her face taut.
taut.zh: 凯瑟琳显得心绪不宁，脸色紧张。

tax.en: He already pays 40% tax on his income.
Many people feel they are paying too much tax.

taxi.en: They sent me home in a taxi.
taxi.zh: 他们用出租车把我送回家。

taxi.en: We took a taxi to the hotel.

tea.en: Would you like a cup of tea or coffee?
tea.zh: 你想来一杯茶还是咖啡？

tea.en: Do you take milk and sugar in your tea?
tea.zh: 你的茶里面要放牛奶和糖吗？

teach.en: Neil teaches at the Guildhall School of Music in London.
teach.zh: 尼尔在伦敦吉尔德霍尔音乐学校教书。

teach.en: He taught geography at the local secondary school.
teach.zh: 他在当地中学教授地理。

teacher.en: The teacher sent him to the principal’s office.
teacher.zh: 那位老师叫他去校长办公室。

teacher.en: They hired a tutor to help him with his English.
teacher.zh: 他们请了一位家教来教他英语。

teaching.en: Mrs Ward had many years of experience in teaching.
teaching.zh: 沃德太太拥有多年教学经验。

teaching.en: She’s thinking of going into teaching (=becoming a teacher).

team.en: Bobby Charlton was in the team that won the World Cup.

tear.en: The children were all in tears.
She came home in floods of tears.
tear.zh: 她泪流满面地回到家里。

tease.en: Don’t get upset. I was only teasing.
tease.zh: 别生气，我只是在逗你玩。

tease.en: He used to tease her mercilessly.
tease.zh: 他过去总是无情地取笑她。

technical.en: Our staff will be available to give you technical support.
technical.zh: 有我们的员工向你提供技术支持。

technical.en: I have no technical knowledge at all.
technical.zh: 我一点技术知识都没有。

technician.en: Whether he was a great artist or not, Dali was a superb technician.
technician.zh: 不管达利是不是一位伟大的艺术家，他肯定是一个卓越的技巧大师。

technique.en: There are various techniques for dealing with industrial pollution.
technique.zh: 处理工业污染有很多不同的技术。

technique.en: In mathematics, we use many techniques of problem-solving.
technique.zh: 在数学中，我们会使用多种方法解题。

technological.en: The steam engine was the greatest technological advance of the 19th century
